name: v0.49.35
body:
# v0.49.35

This patch makes long OpenCode 2 sessions faster by letting OpenCode fold its own stored history while the session is idle, starts emergency recovery when OpenCode 2 reports an overflow as a failed step, keeps the context limit steady across a plugin reload, moves more `ctx_expand` work off OpenCode 2's main thread, fixes Oh My Pi turns refused after tag renumbering, and lets subagent sessions reclaim more context.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode or Pi after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Long OpenCode 2 sessions got slower with every message (#632, thanks @moynzzz):** OpenCode 2 loads a session's whole stored history on every step, and Magic Context trimmed it afterwards, so a long session paid for its full history each time. When a long session goes idle, Magic Context now asks OpenCode to fold its stored history behind a checkpoint, and OpenCode loads only what follows it. On a 25,000-message test session, a step dropped from 1.3–2.0 seconds to 0.33–0.49 seconds. What the model receives is unchanged, and so is the prompt cache.
- **Emergency recovery didn't start on an OpenCode 2 overflow (#827, thanks @tobwen):** Magic Context only noticed a "context too large" rejection when it arrived as an HTTP error. With OpenAI's Responses API, the same error can arrive inside a streamed response, which OpenCode 2 reports as a failed step. Those failed steps now start recovery too.
- **A plugin reload forced a full prompt rebuild on OpenCode (#826, thanks @iceteaSA):** after a reload, the first pass used the model's catalog limit instead of the session's proven context limit, and the smaller budget rebuilt the whole cached prompt. The proven limit is now kept across the reload. A real drop in capacity, such as a model change or an overflow, still rebuilds once.
- **`ctx_expand` still blocked OpenCode 2's main thread (#825, thanks @iceteaSA):** looking up raw message positions ran on the serving thread, and its cost grew with the session's length instead of the range expanded. Those lookups now run on a background thread, by row position, and so do range expansions. The output is unchanged.
- **Oh My Pi turns refused after tag renumbering (#778, thanks @sisttri):** with OpenAI's Responses API, a renumbered session could keep an old tag number in the stored copy of a signed reply, and Oh My Pi's dispatch check then refused every turn. Magic Context now removes that stale number from the stored copy, only on a pass that is already rebuilding the cached prompt, and replays the same decision on later passes.
- **Subagent sessions kept old tool-call skeletons (#643, thanks @dhaern):** in a subagent session, dropped tool calls outside the newest 20 now become full removals instead of short skeletons, on a pass that is already rebuilding the cached prompt. That frees more context in long subagent runs. Primary sessions are unchanged.
- **`ctx_expand` gave no useful answer for a file or image whose content wasn't kept (#780, thanks @null-axiom):** it returned only the part's name. It now says plainly that the content wasn't kept, with the file's name, type and stored location when known, and suggests asking the user to attach it again. It never prints inline file data.
- **Summaries could carry commit hashes from outside their range (#774, thanks @null-axiom):** a hash in a summary is now kept only if it appears in the messages that summary covers. Plain numbers are never treated as hashes. When a session's stored history is renumbered, inline message labels in summaries now move with it, but only when the shift is certain.

## Logging

- **Auto-search explains its decisions (#773, thanks @null-axiom):** each automatic memory search now logs one line with its outcome, the top score in each search lane, the near misses below the threshold, the search pool's state and the time taken. No query or memory text is logged.
- **Clearer logs when a summary times out (#828, thanks @dhaern):** the logs now say which parts of the request made the size estimate incomplete, and the summarizer timeout line says what was waiting.

name: v0.49.34
body:
# v0.49.34

This patch stops OpenCode 1 sessions from ending up with two summary markers after a failed save.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **A failed save could leave a second summary marker on OpenCode 1:** when Magic Context moves the point OpenCode loads history from, it writes a marker into OpenCode's database and then records that marker in its own database. If the second write failed, the next history update didn't know the first marker was its own and added another. Magic Context now records the marker it intends to write before writing it, and the next update adopts a marker that's already in place instead of adding one. Cases it can't settle with certainty are logged and left untouched.
  - **Cleanup of leftover markers** now runs only on a pass that is already rebuilding the cached prompt, so it can never change what a cached request loads.
  - **OpenCode 2 and Pi:** unchanged. They don't use this marker.

name: Dashboard dashboard-v0.20.23
body:
## Dashboard v0.20.23

The Cache page keeps reading Broca runs once Broca starts recording how a run and Magic Context agreed on the shape of history edits. Without this update, those runs would stop showing their steps and usage. Works with Magic Context 0.49.x.

name: v0.49.33
body:
# v0.49.33

This patch stops OpenCode 2 sessions from paying two full prompt-cache writes when their tool list changes.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **A tool-list change cost two full cache writes on OpenCode 2 (#819, thanks @iceteaSA):** when a plugin reload added, removed or renamed tools, the provider lost its cached prompt on the next request, but Magic Context treated that pass as a cache hit. Its history head stayed as it was and its queued drops stayed held, so each session paid a second full write later, when those drops finally landed. On OpenCode 2, a change to the names or descriptions of the tools a session sends now rebuilds the history head once, and the queued drops and cleanup land in that same rebuild.
  - **Upgrading:** the first pass after the upgrade records each session's tool list without rebuilding.
  - **Schema-only differences:** a change to a tool's schema alone never counts, so it can't cause a rebuild that the provider wouldn't already pay for.
  - **Known limits:** a plugin that changes the tool list after Magic Context's hook isn't seen. A tool entry that OpenCode drops before sending can still cause one rebuild when its description changes.
  - **OpenCode 1 and Pi:** unchanged. Their tool-list signal is shared by every session in the process, so it still isn't used.

name: v0.49.32
body:
# v0.49.32

This patch stops Pi's `ctx_search` from returning messages from a branch you left with `/tree`, and removes three more reads that blocked OpenCode's main thread while nothing had changed.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode or Pi after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Pi search returned messages from an abandoned branch (#807, thanks @LioTree):** after `/tree` moved to another branch and the session continued, `ctx_search` could return messages from the branch you left, once later summaries passed their message numbers. A branch change on Pi and Oh My Pi now rebuilds that session's message search index from the active branch, the same way OpenCode 2 already does after a revert. Until the rebuild finishes, message search returns no message results, and a search or automatic hint already in flight drops any message result from the old branch. Memories, notes, summaries and git results are unaffected.
- **Three OpenCode reads repeated when nothing had changed (#825, thanks @iceteaSA):**
  - **Dream backlog counts:** the sidebar recounted the dreamer's pending work on every poll, because any database write reset its cache. The sidebar and status display now reuse a count for up to 60 seconds. The dreamer's own scheduling still uses exact counts.
  - **Chunk coverage:** the check rebuilt each summary's search text from the index even when nothing in it had changed. It now reuses the previous result while the summary and its indexed messages are unchanged, and rebuilds as soon as either changes.
  - **Mis-scoped chunk scan:** every project registration, including each plugin reload, rescanned for misfiled search chunks. A finished scan is now remembered per project and embedding model, and runs again after a session's project changes.

  None of these changes what the model sees.

name: v0.49.31
body:
# v0.49.31

This patch fixes four Oh My Pi and Pi problems from one detailed report, stops an OpenCode 2 `/goal` compaction from pushing every request past the context window, lets very large Pi sessions run without refusals, shortens how long Pi holds the database lock when queued drops land, and makes the dreamer's verify and memory-mapping tasks stop failing on valid answers.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode or Pi after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Every Oh My Pi turn refused after local midnight (#820, thanks @TheOrdinaryWow):** Oh My Pi adds a date and folder reminder row to the request after Magic Context has checked the turn's structure, and the check didn't expect it. From midnight on, every turn was refused until Oh My Pi restarted. The check now accepts that reminder only when it matches Oh My Pi's exact template, with a valid date and the session's own folder, in the position Oh My Pi uses. Any other extra row is still refused.
- **Oh My Pi Responses turns refused after a matching tag (#821, thanks @TheOrdinaryWow):** when the tag Magic Context re-applies equals the one the model echoed, the reply was prepared without its phase, so every later turn was refused. The phase is now kept in that case.
- **Pi's local embedding preflight never ran (#822, thanks @TheOrdinaryWow):** an early return skipped the pooling check, so session backfill retried every minute and never finished. The check now runs.
- **A Pi log line printed `[object Object]` (#823, thanks @TheOrdinaryWow):** the historian's fallback models now print by name.
- **OpenCode 2 `/goal` could push every request past the context window (#824, thanks @elmagow):** when OpenCode 2 compacts a long session, it adds a "recent context" block of raw conversation to its checkpoint, and in an agent session that block could reach millions of tokens. It was then sent on every request, and reverting didn't remove it. Magic Context already serves those messages itself, so on OpenCode 2.1 and newer its compaction answer now asks for no recent-context block. Sessions already affected, and OpenCode 2.0, have the block trimmed before the request is sent, and every request carrying a checkpoint is measured against the window first. No message that wasn't summarized yet is lost.
- **Very large Pi sessions were refused:** Pi sessions with around 200,000 or more tags could be refused, because a memory estimate counted far more than the session uses and tagging took too long. Sessions up to 250,000 tags now run, and the requests sent are unchanged.
- **Pi held the database lock for seconds when queued drops landed:** applying a large batch of queued drops rewrote a stored record once per drop while holding the shared database's write lock, up to about 10 seconds. It is now written once per batch, and the lock is held for a fraction of a second.
- **Pi's retrospective read reminder notices as if the user had written them:** it now strips them, as OpenCode already did.
- **Dreamer verify ignored `timeout_minutes`:** verify and verify-broad cut every batch at 4 minutes, whatever the configured task timeout, so slow models never finished a batch. They now keep starting batches until the configured deadline, and each batch can use the time left.
- **Dreamer memory mapping treated a valid empty answer as a failure:** when a model correctly left every memory in a batch unmapped, as the prompt allows, the answer was rejected and every fallback model was tried in turn. A well-formed empty answer now counts as a completed batch, and those memories retry later on their usual backoff. Malformed answers still fall back.

name: v0.49.30
body:
# v0.49.30

This patch fixes a Pi session stalling on replies its model wrote as blank drop markers, cuts main-thread CPU on long OpenCode 2 sessions, repairs `doctor repair-db`, and adds logging for hidden historian sessions on OpenCode 2.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode or Pi after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Replies written as `[dropped ]` stalled a session (#815, thanks @tevenfeng):** Magic Context removes assistant replies that contain nothing but drop markers, so the model doesn't copy them and stop. It recognized `[dropped]` and `[dropped N]`, but not the blank form `[dropped ]` some models write. Those replies stayed in history and the model kept stopping. All three forms are now removed, with one rule shared by OpenCode and Pi. The removal still happens only on a pass that rebuilds the prompt anyway, so it costs no extra cache write.
- **Main-thread CPU on long OpenCode 2 sessions (#817, thanks @iceteaSA):**
  - **The sidebar usage query:** it read every message of the session on each sidebar poll. It now uses the session index. On the reporter's long sessions, one poll took about 19 ms before and well under a millisecond after.
  - **Message times:** every pass re-read the creation and completion times of every message, although a finished message's times never change. Times are now reused for user messages and finished replies, and re-read only when OpenCode changes or rewrites a message. The times shown to the model are byte-identical.
  - **The history boundary check:** a per-pass check read full summary rows when it needs only two fields. It now reads just those fields.
- **`doctor repair-db` could not salvage a damaged database:** its recovery replay failed on every SQLite version, because the shell's defensive mode blocks the schema writes that recovery needs. Recovery now turns defensive mode off on the fresh replay database only. Every row comes back, along with statistics and search-index definitions. The backup before repair and the integrity checks are unchanged.

## Diagnostics

- **Hidden historian sessions on OpenCode 2 (#818, thanks @Ven0maus):** Magic Context now logs when it creates each hidden historian or dreamer session, and whether it keeps or removes it afterwards. The log also records the `keep_subagents` value in effect at startup. These lines help find why some users see a "session not found" message on OpenCode 2.2.

name: v0.49.29
body:
# v0.49.29

This patch fixes console windows flashing on Windows, OpenCode 2 sessions showing zero tokens, a small config mistake that silently turned memory off, and two cases where Magic Context could change bytes already sent to the model.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode or Pi after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Console windows flashing on Windows (#804, #553, thanks @butterbrodskiy and @devsiac):** the dreamer's verify step ran its git commands without hiding their window, so one verify pass could flash dozens of PowerShell or CMD windows and steal focus. Those commands now run hidden. A test now checks every place Magic Context starts a process, including the ones run through promisified helpers.
- **"Total tokens 0" in the OpenCode 2 sidebar (#805, thanks @maxbrunet):** the sidebar read token totals from OpenCode 1's message table, which is empty on OpenCode 2. It now reads OpenCode 2's own messages.
- **OpenCode 2 dreamer tasks recording zero tokens (#810, thanks @iceteaSA):** on OpenCode 2, the dreamer's tool-using tasks (memory mapping, verify, curate, retrospective) and smart-note evaluation recorded no token usage. They now record the usage their completions report. A memory-mapping batch that times out now keeps the mappings it already produced, instead of reading an empty transcript and losing them.
- **A small config mistake silently turned memory off (#811, thanks @Drynwhyl):** an invalid value anywhere under `memory`, such as an out-of-range `injection_budget_tokens`, marked the whole config untrusted, which turns memory off for a project at its first start. The memory tool then only said "disabled for this project".
  - **What happens now:** an invalid value falls back to its default with a warning, and memory stays on. Only fields that decide which embeddings and which project a memory belongs to (the embedding provider, model and endpoint, the local runtime, the memory switches, home-project admission) still mark the config untrusted, because a wrong value there could delete stored embeddings.
  - **An invalid `git_commit_indexing.max_commits`:** commit indexing keeps working, but deleting old commits pauses until the value is fixed.
  - **When memory is off for this reason:** the memory tool now names the invalid fields.
- **A busy-database fallback could erase a served reminder:** when the database is busy, Magic Context serves its last good request again. Applying newly committed drops to that request also erased reminder text already served on a dropped message, so the request changed and the provider cache rebuilt. Reminders already served now stay until a permitted rebuild. Normal passes still render every drop as the plain placeholder.
- **OpenCode 2.2.0 instruction updates:** OpenCode 2.2.0 lets plugins post instruction updates mid-conversation as system rows.
  - **The summarizer** no longer reads those rows as something you said.
  - **The busy-database fallback** now works in sessions that contain them. An update that arrives right after such a fallback is no longer dropped, and an instruction edited after OpenCode's checkpoint now makes the fallback refuse instead of sending the old text.

name: Dashboard dashboard-v0.20.22
body:
## Fixes

- **Memories tab:** category headers now show each project's real memory counts. Before, they counted only the first 200 memories loaded. Every memory can now be reached by paging, and a list that's cut short says how many are shown out of the total.
- **Memory mural:** the mural image now displays. Before, the box stayed blank even after the mural rendered.

name: v0.49.28
body:
# v0.49.28

This patch fixes two dreamer problems: memory mapping falling behind in large projects, and Pi dreamer tasks stopping at 30 minutes regardless of their configured timeout.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode or Pi after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Memory mapping falling behind (#809, thanks @iceteaSA):** the dreamer maps memories to source files in batches of five, each given a fixed four-minute slice. In projects where a batch regularly needs close to four minutes, two timed-out batches in a row stopped the night's run, so only a few memories were mapped each night and the backlog kept growing.
  - **What happens now:** a timed-out batch is split into smaller batches (five becomes two, two and one), and those run straight away in the same run. Mappings a timed-out batch already saved are kept, and only the rest are retried.
  - **When a run still stops:** only after a single memory times out twice in a row with nothing saved.
  - **Settings:** none added. The per-batch slice and the task timeout are unchanged.
  - **Hosts:** OpenCode and Pi.
- **Pi dreamer tasks stopping at 30 minutes (#784, PR #808, thanks @izhangzhihao and @mvanhorn):** on Pi and Oh My Pi, each dreamer task runs in a child process that was always stopped after 30 minutes, so a task configured with a longer `timeout_minutes` was cut off early. The child process now gets the task's own timeout plus five minutes, so the dreamer's timeout always decides and reports the right reason. The user-memory review task now uses its own configured timeout too.

name: v0.49.27
body:
# v0.49.27

This patch stops Magic Context from deleting data for sessions another OpenCode instance owns, and fixes four smaller issues: a historian retry loop, an OpenCode 2 memory leak, a Windows doctor false refusal, and a dreamer check that threw away good results.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode or Pi after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Sessions deleted when several OpenCode instances share one store (#782, thanks @OlegAndreych):** a background sweep treated any session missing from the local OpenCode database as deleted and removed its Magic Context data, including its history summaries. When several OpenCode instances share one Magic Context store, for example in Docker sandboxes or with separate data folders, each instance deleted the others' idle sessions.
  - **The sweep is gone.** Magic Context no longer deletes a session's data because it can't find the session.
  - **What still deletes data:** deleting a session in OpenCode cleans up its Magic Context data, as before.
  - **Sessions you deleted while Magic Context wasn't running:** their data now stays in the store.
- **Historian retrying the same failed chunk (#802, thanks @manorit2001):** when a historian run finished without being able to publish anything, the next trigger could send the same messages to the model again, paying for the same rejection each time.
  - **What happens now:** after such a run, automatic runs wait until the session has a newer message.
  - **What still runs:** the near-full-context and emergency paths still get one attempt, and `/ctx-recomp` and wrap-up work as before.
  - **Hosts:** OpenCode and Pi.
- **OpenCode 2 holding the first request's messages in memory (#800, thanks @null-axiom):** the transform kept a reference to the first request's full message list, attachments included, for the server's whole lifetime, once per OpenCode 2 location. Each request's messages are now released when the request ends. What is sent to the model doesn't change.
- **Windows doctor refusing because of its own command line (#799, thanks @mcheiyue):** doctor checks that no host process holds the database before opening it. On Windows it matched "opencode" anywhere in a process's command line, so `doctor --harness opencode`, or any tool started with a path like `D:\OpenCode`, counted as a running host. Doctor now recognizes a host by the program it runs, or by the script Node, Bun or Deno runs, never by argument values. A process doctor can't identify still blocks the check, as before.
- **Dreamer discarding a valid memory check (#803, thanks @Harry-zklcdc):** a correct verification reply can be very short when it covers a single memory. The dreamer treated any reply of 32 tokens or fewer as a provider outage before reading it, discarded it, and tried the fallback models. It now accepts a complete, well-formed reply that covers exactly the memories it asked about. A short reply that's malformed or covers the wrong memories still counts as an outage.

name: v0.49.26
body:
# v0.49.26

This patch stops Magic Context from serving an old copy of text another OpenCode plugin adds to your messages. It also stops the historian from occasionally skipping or repeating a message on OpenCode 1.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Text another plugin adds on OpenCode 1:** some plugins add a text part to the current message on every step, for example a marker that changes from step to step. Magic Context treated that part as part of the conversation: it numbered it, saved its text, and on later steps put the saved copy back. The plugin's current text was replaced by an older one, which the plugin could then refuse.
  - **New parts:** text another plugin adds is now left exactly as that plugin wrote it. It's never numbered, saved or restored, and `ctx_reduce` skips its id.
  - **Existing sessions:** a part an older release already numbered keeps the bytes that release sent while the plugin's text is unchanged, so the upgrade doesn't break the prompt cache.

  OpenCode 2, Pi and Oh My Pi are unaffected.
- **Historian skipping or repeating a message on OpenCode 1:** Magic Context keeps a running count of each session's messages. OpenCode orders messages by when they were created, not when they were saved, so a message saved a few milliseconds late could be left out of that count until OpenCode restarted. The historian started each new chunk from the stored count, so it could skip one message for good, then summarize another twice after the restart. Now:
  - **Where the historian continues:** it starts after the last message it summarized, found by that message's id.
  - **Detecting a late save:** the count notices a message saved late and rebuilds itself. The check looks only at rows written since the last check, so it costs the same however long the session is.
  - **A wrong count found mid-run:** the run ends without publishing a summary and tries again once the count is rebuilt.

  Messages skipped before this release stay unsummarized. They are still in the session, and `ctx_expand` and `ctx_search` can read them.

name: v0.49.25
body:
# v0.49.25

This patch stops tool definitions from inflating Magic Context's token count and removes a whole-history copy from every turn of a Claude session with thinking on.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode, Pi or Oh My Pi after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Tool definitions counted once for every tool ever seen:** on OpenCode, Magic Context added up every tool it had seen for a model and agent, across all sessions and projects, and never dropped one. After a restart this could make a session look full when it wasn't: a session at 76% could read as 98%, which triggered emergency cleanup and a cache rebuild. It also inflated the "Tool Defs" figure in the sidebar.
  - **OpenCode 2:** the count now uses exactly the tools the current request carries.
  - **OpenCode 1:** it counts the tools the model was offered recently. A tool stops counting once the model has been in use for about 10 minutes without it, and time spent idle doesn't count.

  Thanks to @jjjermiah.
- **Doctor on OpenCode 2:** the local embedding check now looks at the plugin copy OpenCode 2 actually loads.
- **Thinking sessions:** every turn of a Claude session with thinking on copied the whole message history in case a rare retry needed it. The copy is now taken only on turns where that retry can run. On large sessions this saves tens of milliseconds per turn. Thanks to @iceteaSA.

name: v0.49.24
body:
# v0.49.24

This patch fixes several ways Oh My Pi could refuse every turn, keeps memory and note tool calls working on providers that drop optional arguments, and fixes two cases where the summarizer stopped summarizing.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode, Pi or Oh My Pi after updating. No database migration is needed.
- The `ctx_memory` and `ctx_note` tool definitions change in this release, so each open session rebuilds its prompt cache once, on its next turn.

## Fixed

- **Oh My Pi:** each of these left a session refusing every turn until a new session was started.
  - Resumed sessions were refused when Oh My Pi added a tool-control message to the request. Thanks to @tsankotsanev, who also sent the fix in #786.
  - Dropping a tool call could leave two assistant messages next to each other, and Oh My Pi's `Continue.` repair message wasn't expected. Thanks to @TheOrdinaryWow.
  - The first turn after a restart was refused when another session's background preparation was cancelled, including when several subagents started at once. Thanks to @Zireael.
  - A chained continuation was refused after a summary was folded into the history, because the history block's timestamps changed. Thanks to @Zireael.
  - A message typed while the agent was working was refused, because Oh My Pi's steering wrapper wasn't expected. Thanks to @Zireael.
  - After an aborted turn, every Claude turn was refused, because Oh My Pi drops an empty aborted reply that Magic Context still expected. Thanks to @TheOrdinaryWow.
- **`ctx_memory` and `ctx_note` on providers that drop optional arguments:** some providers, such as InferenceNet on OpenRouter, send only the first argument when a tool marks nothing as required, so almost every call failed. The key arguments are now required. Values that don't apply to an action can be sent empty, and when updating or merging a memory the model passes its current category to keep it. Thanks to @garionberg.
- **Summarizer:**
  - A session that runs from a single prompt is summarized again once it passes the execute threshold, instead of waiting for the 85% force band. Thanks to @yelrom-liively.
  - After an OpenCode session leaves Rust transform mode, the summarizer no longer refuses forever on gaps left by notification-only messages. Thanks to @iceteaSA.
- **Task permissions:** a task permission that denies everything and then allows named agents no longer hides the Task tool. Thanks to @selfagency for the report and @DreamchaserLG for the fix in #787.

## Changed

- When you answer a question that an Alfonso agent asked you, the summarizer now records your answer as your own words instead of dropping it with other system notices.

name: Dashboard dashboard-v0.20.21
body:
## Dashboard 0.20.21

Reads Broca logs that use one new log feature:

- `output-reservation/v1`: a record written before a step whose output cap Broca lowered so the request fits the model's window.

The dashboard doesn't use this record. Without this release, it stops reading a Broca log at the first record that requires the feature, and the steps after that point don't show.

name: Dashboard dashboard-v0.20.20
body:
## Dashboard 0.20.20

Reads Broca logs that use two new log features:

- `provider-fallback-block/v1`: a message can carry a part recording a provider's server-side switch to another model.
- `refusal-fallback/v1`: a refused model step is recorded, and a finished step can say which model actually served it.

The dashboard doesn't use these fields, and a run that carries them keeps all its steps and usage. Without this release, the dashboard stops reading a Broca log at the first record that requires one of these features.

name: Dashboard dashboard-v0.20.19
body:
## Dashboard 0.20.19

Reads Broca logs that use one new log feature:

- `tool-schema-pins/v1`: a run's plan manifest records the tool schema pins it froze.

The dashboard doesn't use this field. Without this release, it stops reading a Broca log at the first record that requires it, and the steps after that point don't show.

name: v0.49.23
body:
# v0.49.23

This patch makes sure Magic Context's background runs on Oh My Pi can only use the tools they are given.

## Upgrading

- Restart Oh My Pi after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- On Oh My Pi, Magic Context's background runs (the summarizer, the dreamer and their helpers) are meant to run with no tools, or with a short read-only list. Oh My Pi applied that restriction to its built-in tools only, so tools from extensions you have installed were still offered to those runs and could be called. Each background run now gets exactly its own tool list, and starts no run at all if the restriction can't be applied. Your extensions still load, so provider and sign-in extensions keep working. Pi was not affected.

name: v0.49.22
body:
# v0.49.22

This patch keeps Oh My Pi summarizer and dreamer runs working when the conversation they read mentions a file or a URL with `@`.

## Upgrading

- Restart Oh My Pi after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- Oh My Pi summarizer and dreamer runs no longer fail or attach files when the transcript they read contains `@` mentions such as `@skill://name` or a file path. Mentions stay literal text, and memories they write keep a plain `@` (#779, thanks @Qiiks).

name: v0.49.21
body:
# v0.49.21

This patch makes Pi and Oh My Pi sessions more reliable and releases idle local embedding memory. It also adds optional hosted search reranking and improves documentation-maintenance fallbacks.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode, Pi, or Oh My Pi after updating. No database migration is needed.

## New

- Optionally configure hosted `ctx_search` reranking with a user-level [`rerank` block](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/blob/master/CONFIGURATION.md); local reranking remains the default (#765, thanks @XWIlluDelu).

## Fixed

- Oh My Pi sessions continue after tag-prefix cleanup, including saved history and forks (#766, thanks @sisttri and @Qiiks).
- Local embedding processes stop after ten idle minutes and restart on demand. OpenCode 2 releases embeddings when their last context closes (#767, thanks @LouisLau-art).
- Documentation maintenance tries the configured fallback model for invalid proposal JSON and recognizes formatted empty proposals as no changes (#768, thanks @breakbeatkid).
- Older Pi and Oh My Pi sessions no longer refuse turns after their first local tag update (#769, thanks @sisttri).
- Pi and Oh My Pi limit database lock waits to the remaining turn budget instead of leaving turns stuck (#770, thanks @andrewsoonqn).
- `map-memories` no longer promises a fallback attempt when the remaining budget cannot allow it (#771, thanks @breakbeatkid).
- Pi sessions no longer refuse turns immediately after another session's slow tag loading fails.
- OpenCode 2 message search keeps up with long sessions, catches up on previously missed messages, and reflects reverted history (#772, thanks @null-axiom).
- Oh My Pi no longer refuses turns after switching models when an earlier reply was interrupted during thinking (#686, thanks @Qiiks for the report and @Zireael for the test case).
- Replies containing only a copied tag no longer send an empty part that strict OpenAI-compatible providers reject, and affected sessions recover automatically (#775, thanks @yongwun).
- Updated Zod to 4.6.7 to address a memory-exhaustion vulnerability in collection validation.

name: Dashboard dashboard-v0.20.18
body:
## Dashboard 0.20.18

Reads Broca logs that use three new log features:

- `provider-declarations/v1`: a run's plan manifest records the result formats and `late_results` capability its tool providers declare.
- `provider-held/v1`: held tool-call records and a `tool_held` pause reason.
- `plan-reference-slots/v1`: a run's plan manifest records the reference slots its tools declare.

The dashboard doesn't use these fields. Without this release, it stops reading a Broca log at the first record that requires one of them, and the steps after that point don't show.

name: v0.49.20
body:
# v0.49.20

## Fixed

- OpenCode 2 replays the last good request when its database is busy instead of sending an incomplete context.
- Signed-thinking requests keep their accepted prefix across disabled compaction, mode switches, date rollover after restart, and idle passes.
- Oh My Pi keeps Magic Context's `ctx_*` tools at the top level with their complete descriptions and schemas instead of hiding them behind the `xd://` catalog. Missing `ctx_reduce.drop` arguments show an example range (#756, thanks @TheOrdinaryWow for the report and transcript scan).
- Local embeddings follow each model's declared pooling and normalization, including CLS pooling for BGE models. Memories and git commits re-embed in the background; inactive-session history vectors stay out of semantic search until that session runs `/ctx-embed start` (#753, thanks @LouisLau-art).
- OpenCode 2 caps its saved request copies for side questions so memory use no longer grows with every session opened since the server started (#764, thanks @null-axiom).
- Primary sessions on OpenCode 1, OpenCode 2 and Pi no longer strand queued reductions below force pressure. When only the current user prompt prevents summarization, the next pass may summarize past it once. Otherwise, eligible reductions and cleanup can apply together after 2% reclaim or three held execute passes, provided no summary is running or waiting to render. Token limits, tool-call boundaries and signed-thinking safety remain in force; Rust mode is unchanged.
- Dreamer detects first model activity on OpenCode 2, Pi and Oh My Pi. A completely silent primary with a configured fallback stops after 90 seconds, leaving the remaining task time for the fallback; a primary streaming text, reasoning or tool calls keeps its full timeout.
- Semantic auto-search keeps its warm history-vector pool after a hint's one-second deadline and loads only new or changed vectors between turns. Cold vectors no longer block a turn, hints list fragments by relevance, disabled memory skips background memory work, and cancelled `ctx_search` calls stop loading history vectors (#762, thanks @null-axiom for the report and detailed trace).
- OpenCode maintenance sweeps empty recovery-lock folders without removing held locks, resumes previously parked OpenCode 2 orphan sweeps, and retires tag-revision metadata when sessions are permanently deleted. Repeated tag-floor, nudge-evaluation and scheduler-hold diagnostics log on state changes rather than every pass (#746, thanks @null-axiom).

## Changed

- Failed historian and dreamer attempts retain their attempted model and sanitized host error in the Historian tab. Silent-model timeouts record why the attempt stopped, and unknown configured models warn once per process.
- Auto-search deadline diagnostics include per-step timings and attached-hint relevance scores. Background workers shut down without leaving pending requests or resources behind.

name: v0.49.19
body:
# v0.49.19

This patch release fixes Pi and Oh My Pi on Bun 1.3.x, `ctx_expand` by tag in Rust transform mode, dreamer runs stuck on a model that never answers, four edge cases of the signed-thinking hold, and a migration risk on Bun 1.4.4.

## Upgrading

- **No migration.** `context.db` stays at schema 95 and `store.db` at schema 63. Restart OpenCode 1, OpenCode 2, Pi or Oh My Pi after updating.

## Fixed

- Pi and Oh My Pi running on Bun 1.3.x (Oh My Pi's documented minimum is Bun 1.3.14) no longer refuse every turn on long sessions after 10 seconds. Bun releases before 1.4 hold back every message to a background worker until the worker's startup code has finished, and the worker that loads a session's tags waited for such a message during startup, so it never finished. Semantic auto-search hints had the same problem on that Bun and always came back empty; they now return matches again. Bun 1.4 and Node were not affected (issue 754, thanks @ChenYCL for the report and the investigation).
- In Rust transform mode, `ctx_expand` with a tag number now refuses and points to expanding by message or range, instead of returning an unrelated old item. Tag numbers in Rust mode come from the module's own store and can repeat numbers left over from before the session switched modes. TypeScript mode, Pi and Oh My Pi are unchanged.
- On OpenCode 1, a dreamer task whose primary model never produces any output (for example a free model that has stopped answering) now moves to the configured fallback model after 90 seconds of silence, instead of holding the run for up to 20 minutes and then failing. This applies to classification, memory mapping and verification, and only when a fallback model is configured. A model that is answering, however slowly, keeps its full time.
- Four edge cases of the hold on Claude models whose thinking is bound to the prompt prefix:
  - With compaction turned off, the first request after a restart could put a new prompt head in front of the open turn's signed thinking. That thinking is now removed from the request when the head may have changed, on OpenCode 1, OpenCode 2, Pi and Oh My Pi.
  - After a restart, messages that a recovered request had sent untagged stay untagged until a pass that may rewrite the prompt anyway, so a deferred pass after the restart sends the same bytes.
  - When a session has been idle past its cache lifetime while the open turn's signed thinking is held, the date in the system prompt is no longer advanced on that request; it advances on the first request that doesn't keep the held thinking.
  - The refusal that keeps an oversized request from going out with held signed thinking now applies only to requests that actually hold it. Other requests are sized and refused the same way as for any other model.
- Upgrading on Bun 1.4.4 no longer risks memory and note writes failing if an upgrade stops partway through the database migrations.

name: v0.49.18
body:
# v0.49.18

This patch release fixes a repeated cache bust after cleanup on OpenCode 2, false dispatch refusals on Oh My Pi, tag numbering around file attachments, section references in the tag cleaner, compaction during long Claude turns, and context sizing on the first pass after a host restart.

## Upgrading

- **No migration.** `context.db` stays at schema 95 and `store.db` at schema 63. Restart OpenCode 1, OpenCode 2, Pi or Oh My Pi after updating.

## Fixed

- On OpenCode 2, a cleanup pass is no longer followed by a second cache bust on the next request: instruction rows already covered by the history summary are now served on every pass, so the pass after a cleanup sends the same bytes (issue 750, thanks @null-axiom).
- Pi and Oh My Pi no longer refuse valid requests with `comparison=role` when a tool call was interrupted by another message. The dispatch check now models the host moving the tool result forward into the call's window, but only on providers where Oh My Pi itself does that (issue 751, thanks @Zireael).
- New OpenCode file attachments no longer take a tag number, so the next visible number the model sees is the one its reply gets. Token totals for messages that mix text and files are also corrected in the sidebar and in protected-tail sizing.
- The tag cleaner no longer drops the leading digit of a section reference such as `§12.3`. A session with a text part that starts with such a reference has its prompt cache rewritten once, from that part on, the first time this version serves it.
- Long autonomous turns on Claude models whose thinking is bound to the prompt prefix now compact at the normal threshold, instead of staying at 85-99% until the next user message. Compaction is held only right after heavy reasoning, on OpenCode 1, OpenCode 2, Pi and Oh My Pi (issue 729, thanks @moynzzz).
- After a host restart, the first pass no longer sizes context usage with the fit-check estimate, which could double the reading for models missing from the tokenizer calibration table and land queued or emergency drops on a pass that should have deferred (issue 752, thanks @Sugaroverdose).

## Docs

- The configuration reference's context-management section now explains that a `cache_ttl` shorter than the provider's real cache lifetime (for example a locally hosted model whose prefix cache doesn't expire) makes idle expiry rebuild onto a cache that is still warm, so `cache_ttl` should match the provider.

name: v0.49.17
body:
# v0.49.17

This patch release improves stopped-store reads, adds OpenCode 2.1.0 support, and fixes search, summarization, event handling, logging and storage cleanup.

## Upgrading

- **No migration.** `context.db` stays at schema 95 and `store.db` at schema 63. Restart OpenCode 1, OpenCode 2, Pi or Oh My Pi after updating.

## Fixed

- Oh My Pi compaction markers now retain a resolvable history boundary, verify writes and avoid duplicate host summaries (issue 748, thanks @Qiiks).
- Doctor can inspect a fully stopped SQLite store without changing its contents.
- OpenCode 2.1.0 native replay metadata and checkpoints are supported. Once OpenCode 2.1.0 compacts a session, OpenCode 2.0.x can't open it again.
- Automatic search hints now wait for embeddings only within a latency budget, preserve real relevance scores, exclude the live tail and show readable matched fragments (issue 743, thanks @null-axiom).
- Summarizer runs on OpenCode 2 and Pi cost less: a first attempt now writes only the system prompt to the prompt cache, because the rest of each summarizer request changes every run and was written but never read back (issue 744, thanks @null-axiom).
- The OpenCode 2 event loop keeps processing events after a handler error, and a deleted-session sweep recovers missed cleanup (issue 745, thanks @null-axiom).
- Transform timing logs summarize each pass while retaining individual slow stages; system-prompt changes report element hashes, byte lengths and offsets without logging prompt content (issue 746, thanks @null-axiom).
- Stale project identities are removed only when their directories are definitely gone. Session deletion avoids unnecessary fence locks and removes empty lock directories; RPC startup reaps dead discovery records and shutdown prunes empty discovery directories (issue 746, thanks @null-axiom).
- Background embedding work yields after repeated rate limits, and commit-embedding sweeps stop at their five-minute deadline (issue 746, thanks @null-axiom).
- Non-git projects skip commit probes and log once per parking interval instead of on every maintenance tick (issue 747, thanks @null-axiom). Maintenance ticks also use a label that does not imply a dreamer prefix (issue 746, thanks @null-axiom).
- Long sessions no longer stall for seconds when many queued removals apply at once; queued drops commit in bounded chunks.


## Docs

- Added troubleshooting guidance for the OpenCode 1 Anthropic conversation-ending error (issue 512, thanks @dhaern).

name: v0.49.16
body:
# v0.49.16

This patch release fixes long Pi sessions refusing turns since 0.49.15, keeps summarization on the models you configured, preserves subagent tool results under pressure, and improves long-session recovery and private diagnostic reports. Without a historian model, OpenCode still inherits the session model; Pi and Oh My Pi still do not summarize.

## Upgrading

- **No migration.** `context.db` stays at schema 95 and `store.db` at schema 63. Restart OpenCode 1, OpenCode 2, Pi or Oh My Pi after updating.

## Fixed

- **Long Pi sessions no longer refuse turns while other sessions write to the shared database.** 0.49.15's background tag loading treated any write to the database, from any session, as a sign its pages were outdated, so long sessions could be refused on every turn. Tag loading now checks only the current session for changes, and restarts an outdated load within the existing turn budget.
- Configured historian chains no longer fall back to the active session model when exhausted (issue 740, thanks @chpock).
- Historian calls no longer accept a provider's model suggestion, so a misspelled or unknown model can't be swapped for an unconfigured one (issue 744, thanks @null-axiom).
- **Subagent tool results stay intact when an emergency reduction cannot fit.** An impossible protected-history floor no longer silently drops tool results, and a refused reduction stays refused on retry (issue 731, thanks @tppawelgrzesik).
- **Historian repair prompts explain when a chunk is complete.** When all messages in a chunk are covered, repair requests place `<unprocessed_from>` after that chunk's last message. Pi fallback models receive the same repair prompt (issue 727, thanks @null-axiom).
- **`doctor --issue` keeps your own explanation and the diagnostic error wording.** Project paths, ids and message content stay masked or aliased in the report, so real project names and directories are not exposed (issue 732, thanks @tppawelgrzesik).
- **Oh My Pi accepts system notices in the middle of history.** Positioned `role: system` rows no longer break managed requests or WebSocket continuations (issue 686, thanks @Qiiks, @Zireael and @IdealBoy709).
- **OpenCode 2 refreshes model limits after a provider reload.** The next request uses the updated context limit instead of a stale cached value (issue 741, contributed in PR 742 by @tobwen).
- **`ctx_expand` no longer freezes OpenCode while reading archived history.** Archive searches avoid a global full-text scan, and raw ordinal reads run off the main thread.

name: Dashboard dashboard-v0.20.10
body:
This release makes the Config page readable by screen readers and accessibility tools, and keeps the dashboard reading Broca sessions as Broca records more detail about failed runs and ChatGPT requests.

## Fixed

- **The Config page now announces which option is selected.** The Embedding Provider buttons work as a radio group, so the active provider is announced as selected, and the arrow keys move between options. The User/Project Config and background-model harness tabs announce which one is active. Nothing changes visually.
- **Pop-up pickers say what they're set to.** Output Language and the primary, default and fallback variant pickers now include their current value, or "not set", in the name a screen reader hears. Before, a blank picker and a set one sounded the same.
- **Broca sessions with detailed errors or ChatGPT transport records still open.** Broca can now record Google's structured error details on a failed run, and the request shape of ChatGPT runs. The dashboard recognises both. It reads usage, steps and timestamps, which these records don't change, so session timelines and cache charts stay the same.

name: v0.49.15
body:
# v0.49.15

This patch release fixes tag prefixes in Pi and Oh My Pi, keeps Oh My Pi's WebSocket follow-ups working, and makes background memory work more reliable. There is no database migration.

Pi and Oh My Pi users also get the Pi fixes from 0.49.14, whose Pi package never became installable: damaged session records no longer block a session, refusals name their real cause, long sessions load tags in the background, and an outdated tag load retries automatically. Thanks to @Zireael for the report in issue 723.

## Upgrading

- **No migration.** `context.db` stays at schema 95 and `store.db` at schema 63. Restart OpenCode 1, OpenCode 2, Pi or Oh My Pi after updating.

## Fixed

- **History compression accepts a chunk that covers every message.** A complete chunk is no longer rejected just because there is no next message left to preserve. The prompt and validation now agree in both TypeScript and Rust modes. Thanks to @null-axiom for the report in issue 727.
- **Pi hides tag prefixes while the model is streaming.** The leading tag no longer flashes in the displayed answer. Oh My Pi now also removes the prefix from saved assistant text; its streaming display cannot yet be changed through the extension API. Thanks to @CodingOX for the report in issue 730.
- **Reloading the OpenCode 2 plugin stops its old background work.** Hidden runs are cancelled when their plugin instance is replaced, and shared database readers close when the last instance releases them. Thanks to @Bearmancer for the report in issue 735.
- **Background Pi requests use a sensible output limit.** Background requests now send the configured output limit, or 32,000 tokens by default, instead of allowing an oversized request that OpenRouter could reject for insufficient credit. Memory verification stops starting new batches at its deadline but gives a batch already running up to two more minutes to finish.
- **Oh My Pi's WebSocket follow-ups keep working.** Follow-up requests and todo reminders no longer fail with "missing current receipt signature" when they continue the session's last managed response and their new items match the prepared request exactly. WebSocket transport is on by default, and turning it off with `providers.openaiWebsockets: "off"` is no longer needed as a workaround. With Hide Secrets on, a follow-up whose new items contain a hidden secret still refuses. Thanks to @Zireael and @IdealBoy709 for the reports and source-level diagnosis in issue 686.
- **Pi's tests no longer interfere with the primer test.** A cached mock from another test no longer changes the primer's result. Thanks to @iceteaSA for diagnosing the test isolation problem in issue 736.

name: v0.49.14
body:
# v0.49.14

This patch release makes Pi recover from damaged session files left by a crash, fixes a long-session stall where history compression never started, and fixes memory mapping on OpenCode 2. It also stops Pi from freezing when it opens a long session for the first time. There is no database migration.

## Upgrading

- **No migration.** `context.db` stays at schema 95 and `store.db` at schema 63. Restart OpenCode 1, OpenCode 2, Pi or Oh My Pi after updating.

## Changed

- **Pi loads a session's tags in the background.** When Pi opens a long session, it now reads that session's tags off the main thread instead of blocking the host for up to several seconds. The first turn waits for the load only within its normal time budget.

## Fixed

- **Pi keeps working after a crash leaves zeros at the end of a session file.** Pi records the tag numbers and request fingerprints it has sent in small per-session files. When a crash left zero bytes at the end of one of them, Pi refused every later turn. Pi now skips that empty tail and repairs it before the next write. It never reuses a tag number it has already sent. When Pi does refuse a turn, the message now names the real cause, and "storage is busy" appears only when another process holds the database lock. Thanks to @Zireael for the report in issue 723, the evidence, and the test fixtures from PR 724.
- **History compression starts again when queued removals cannot apply.** In long sessions, context could stay near 95% because compression was skipped for removals that were queued but could not be applied, such as removals of protected or still-active content. Compression now counts only removals that will really shrink the request. A later step also no longer waits again for a compression run that already ran past its wait time.
- **Memory mapping on OpenCode 2 keeps the model's text across tool calls.** The mapper's text written between tool calls is no longer lost before the final answer is read. Reasoning variants are now found when OpenCode 2 lists them, as versions 2.0.22 and 2.0.32 do. Thanks to @Sivinho for the detailed report in issue 725.

name: Dashboard dashboard-v0.20.9
body:
This release keeps the dashboard reading Broca sessions as Broca records more about how runs end and how sends are handled.

## Fixed

- **Broca sessions with interrupt reasons and send directives still open.** Broca can now record why an interrupted run stopped (for example a runner shutdown) and mark sends that ask to wake a session. The dashboard recognises both records. It reads usage, steps and timestamps, which these records don't change, so session timelines and cache charts stay the same.

The dashboard now recognises these. It reads usage, steps and timestamps, which these records don't change, so session timelines and cache charts stay the same.

name: Dashboard dashboard-v0.20.7

This release keeps the dashboard reading Broca sessions as Broca adds compaction support.

## Fixed

The dashboard now recognises these records. It reads usage, steps and timestamps, which these records don't change, so session timelines and cache charts stay the same.

name: v0.49.13
body:
# v0.49.13

This patch release fixes queued removals after failed turns, bounds memory verification, and restores automatic history re-embedding after an embedding model change. It also reduces unnecessary retrospective calls and fixes memory mapping when a model's answer arrives after its tool calls. There is no database migration.

## Upgrading

- **No migration.** `context.db` stays at schema 95 and `store.db` at schema 63. Restart OpenCode 1, OpenCode 2, Pi or Oh My Pi after updating.
- **Active sessions automatically re-embed their history after an embedding model change.** Old-model embeddings are replaced only for active sessions.

## Changed

- **Memory verification may stop early and save partial results.** It checks five memories at a time, with token limits per batch and run, and a four-minute deadline.
- **The retrospective runs less often.** It calls the model only when a new user message follows an assistant reply, rather than repeatedly reviewing unchanged conversations.

## Fixed

- **Queued removals survive recovery from a failed turn.** The next permitted cache rebuild applies saved drops instead of resending the recovery copy. Thanks to @Qiiks for the report in the issue 713 thread.
- **Pi keeps previously removed thinking out of rebuilt requests.** Recovering a failed turn no longer brings that thinking back during later cache rebuilds.
- **Memory mapping keeps the model's final answer after tool use.** A blank capture no longer rejects a valid answer: the shared check now ignores whitespace-only output before validating it, and Pi keeps the runner's final text after tool-only streams. Thanks to @ICEY16360 for the report in issue 718 and for the shared fix in PR 719.
- **Memory verification reports why it could not finish.** OpenCode 2 verification also gains the code-navigation tools available on other hosts, with guidance to inspect structure before reading full files.

name: Dashboard dashboard-v0.20.6
body:
## Fixes

- **New Broca sessions stay readable.** Broca now records message tags in every new session, and the dashboard reads those sessions instead of showing "no data".

name: Dashboard dashboard-v0.20.5
body:
## Fixes

- **Broca sessions with ordered message delivery stay readable.** Broca's new `delivery-order/v1` session records are now understood, so sessions that use them show their data instead of "no data".

name: v0.49.12
body:
# v0.49.12

This patch release fixes multi-second host freezes on very long OpenCode and Pi sessions. Removing old tool output in Pi no longer causes an extra prompt-cache rebuild, and turning memory off no longer stops unrelated background maintenance. It also fixes startup in new git repositories and improves embedding rate-limit handling. There is no database migration.

## Upgrading

- **No migration.** `context.db` stays at schema 95 and `store.db` at schema 63. Restart OpenCode 1, OpenCode 2, Pi or Oh My Pi after updating.
- **Sessions without a dreamer section rebuild their cache once after the upgrade.** The `ctx_note` tool text changes because it no longer offers smart notes when no dreamer can evaluate them. Tool definitions stay unchanged for configurations with a working dreamer.
- **`memory.enabled: false` now stops only the dreamer's memory tasks.** With the dreamer enabled, smart-note evaluation follows `smart_notes.enabled`, user-memory review follows its own schedule, and docs maintenance follows its own schedule. These tasks keep running with memory off, both on schedule and through `/ctx-dream`.
- **Rust-mode installs should update `ck-mc` to the version shipped with this release.** The Rust module carries the new-repository identity fix and the user-observation collection gate.

## Fixed

- **Very long sessions no longer freeze the host for seconds during a fold.** OpenCode no longer loads every dropped tool's stored content just to apply the fold. Pi and Oh My Pi now look up the recent tool window without loading old tool bodies, and combine pending-drop writes instead of rewriting the same state for every drop.
- **Starting the history summarizer no longer freezes OpenCode for seconds on very long sessions.** Reading the session's message order now runs off the main thread.
- **Queued Pi and Oh My Pi tool drops only ride a real prefix rebuild.** A retry of a deferred compaction marker could incorrectly count as a prefix rebuild and allow tools from earlier requests to be dropped, even though nothing else had changed at the head of the request. Drops now wait for evidence that the prefix is actually being rebuilt, rather than causing an extra cache rewrite themselves. Thanks to @Qiiks for reporting the extra cache rewrites in the issue 713 thread.
- On Claude models that keep signed thinking, tool output the agent removes during a turn now waits for the next real cache rebuild instead of forcing a rebuild on the next message, saving a near-full rewrite of the conversation's cache.
- **Dreamer settings now describe and enforce their real dependencies.** Turning memory off no longer stops unrelated dreamer tasks. `ctx_note` hides smart-note options when the dreamer cannot run, and the historian no longer collects user observations that no dreamer can review. Startup log notes explain settings disabled by another setting. Existing configuration keys stay valid; the descriptions also clarify that auto-search and git commit indexing work with memory off, docs injection works with the dreamer off, and `memory.retrieval_count_promotion_threshold` currently has no effect. Thanks to @null-axiom for the report in issue 715.
- **A new git repository works before its first commit.** Magic Context reads the `.git` files directly to give a repository with no commits a folder identity, without starting git. This avoids the Windows git timeout that could pause memory features in a freshly initialized repository. Thanks to @Mirrowel for the report in issue 717.
- **Embedding rate limits no longer trip the failure breaker.** OpenAI-compatible embedding requests respect `Retry-After` on HTTP 429 responses, or back off when no usable header is supplied, rather than treating rate limits as provider failures.
- **The log warns when an OpenAI-compatible embedding model has no `max_input_tokens` setting.** The default is sized for the bundled local model and can split history into unnecessarily small pieces for other models. The warning explains how to set the model's input limit; changing it re-embeds stored chunks once.
- **Magic Context warns when its storage sits outside Engram's backup folder.** The startup log and `doctor` make the mismatch visible so you can check that the Magic Context data is included in your backups.

name: Dashboard dashboard-v0.20.4
body:
## Fixes

- **Broca sessions that recorded a structured-output downgrade show their data.** Broca now records when a run falls back from provider-enforced structured output. The dashboard reads those sessions instead of showing "no data".

name: Dashboard dashboard-v0.20.3
body:
## Fixes

- **Broca sessions using OpenRouter reasoning show their data.** Broca now records OpenRouter reasoning state in session logs, and the dashboard reads those sessions instead of showing "no data".

name: Dashboard dashboard-v0.20.2
body:
## Fixes

- **Linux AppImage opens on newer systems.** The AppImage bundled old Wayland libraries, so on systems with a newer Mesa the window never opened (`EGL_BAD_ALLOC`). It now uses the system's own Wayland libraries. The workaround with `LD_PRELOAD` is no longer needed. (#716)
- **Memory search finds a memory by its ID.** Typing `1234` or `#1234` shows that memory first, followed by text matches, within the current filters. (#626)
- **Prompt drops in sessions Magic Context doesn't manage are no longer labelled as Magic Context reclaims.** A large drop in, for example, a Broca worker session now reads "Prompt tokens dropped". When the request itself didn't get smaller, it also says that the provider counted fewer tokens.
- **Broca sessions that use newer features show their data.** The dashboard reads sessions that use Broca's structured output and provider text state.

name: v0.49.11
v0.49.10
body:
# v0.49.10

This patch release fixes Oh My Pi sessions on the OpenAI Codex lane that refused every turn after the model's first tool call. There is no database migration.

## Upgrading

- **No migration.** `context.db` stays at schema 95 and `store.db` at schema 63. Restart Oh My Pi after updating. OpenCode and Rust-mode installs are unaffected by this release.

## Fixed

- **Oh My Pi on the Codex lane no longer refuses every turn after a tool call.** Oh My Pi stores each Codex reply exactly as the provider returned it, including its reasoning and tool calls, and sends that stored copy back on later turns. Magic Context's check before sending only recognised stored replies that held just a message, so once the model had called a tool, every later turn was refused at the same point with `comparison=content`. The check now skips stored reasoning and matches tool calls by ID. Every text Magic Context prepared must still match the stored copy exactly, so history it didn't prepare is still refused. Thanks to @Zireael for a detailed report (#714).
- **A refusal caused by an unexpected error inside that check now says where it happened,** instead of reporting a misleading `row=0 … comparison=count`.

name: v0.49.9
body:
# v0.49.9

This patch release stops tool-output cleanup from clearing work that still belongs to the current task, removes a per-turn stall in large sessions, lets free OpenCode Zen models summarize history, and fixes several host and release details. There is no database migration.

## Upgrading

- **No migration.** `context.db` stays at schema 95 and `store.db` at schema 63. Restart OpenCode 1, OpenCode 2, Pi or Oh My Pi after updating.
- **Rust-mode installs need to update `ck-mc` to the version shipped with this release.** The Rust module, not just the host plugin, contains age-based reclaim and the raw-replay fix; the latter prevents a rare large cached-prefix rewrite when a saved replay ends.

## Fixed

- **Tool outputs now count as old by conversation distance:** after three newer user turns, or once newer content fills 25% of the context window. Before, every cache rebuild counted, so two idle gaps of five minutes or a model switch could clear outputs the current task still needed (#700).
- **Large OpenCode and Pi sessions no longer stall on every turn while checking dropped tool outputs.** The check now reads only what the provider receives, not the tool's display data. On Pi's own native API it still reads the full metadata, because that API sends it (#704).
- **Pi no longer rewrites the cached prefix twice in a row after recovering from a saved request.** Cleanup that used to need a second rewrite now lands in the first.
- **OpenCode Zen free models can summarize history on OpenCode 1 and OpenCode 2.** Zen's free tier only accepts requests from OpenCode itself, so on Pi and Oh My Pi those models stay unavailable, and the failure now says so plainly.
- **`/ctx-status` on OpenCode 2 shows the session model's own threshold.** This change was contributed by @manorit2001 in PR #706 (#705).
- **`ck module status` reports the actual `ck-mc` release version (#710).**
- **A smart note whose schedule would run less than once a day is recompiled once with a daily check,** instead of failing every night.
- **Primer candidates sort the same way on every machine,** whatever the system language.

name: v0.49.8
body:
# v0.49.8

This patch release removes long freezes in large OpenCode sessions, fixes a memory leak in Pi, makes summarized-history replay more reliable on OpenCode 2, applies historian limits consistently, and reduces what diagnostic reports share. There is no database migration.

## Upgrading

- **No migration.** `context.db` stays at schema 95 and `store.db` at schema 63. Restart OpenCode 1, OpenCode 2, Pi or Oh My Pi after updating.
- **Some OpenCode 2 sessions have a one-time request-byte change.** Previously omitted host instructions are now retained when replaying summarized history. This can change the cached request prefix once after upgrading; subsequent replays keep those instructions stable (#702).

## Fixed

- **Historian output limits apply to every recompression and wrapup path.** Automatic runs, manual commands and RPC requests now consistently honor `historian.maxTokens`, including Pi and Oh My Pi (#701).
- **OpenCode 2 can replay summarized history when its boundary message is outside the current message window.** A boundary that still exists in the host database can be placed using its saved order, including after moving a session or deleting unrelated old rows. Unsummarized instruction updates remain in the request, and repeated replays do not bring the old history back. Recovery commands also reach the plugin instance for the session's current project (#702).
- **Large OpenCode sessions with many edits no longer freeze for seconds on each turn.** Reapplying dropped tool output used to copy each output's large display-only data every turn; it now copies only what it changes (#703).
- **Pi no longer keeps old turns in memory.** Long-lived workers, timers and connections were created inside a turn and kept that turn's messages alive. They are now created outside any turn, so finished turns can be freed (#707).
- **OpenCode 2 no longer returns the first message for an ordinal beyond the end of a session.** `ctx_expand` reports that the requested message or range is absent, or returns an available search-archive excerpt instead of mislabeling unrelated source text.
- **Slow database work no longer interrupts turns.** The 2-second wait for a locked database now counts only time actually spent waiting for the lock, so slow but uncontended work can't use it up and cause a refusal. A genuinely locked database still refuses safely after 2 seconds.
- **`doctor --issue` reports share less private information on every host.** OpenCode, Pi and Oh My Pi reports use consistent aliases for paths and identifiers and omit free text, source content and tool content. Recent error diagnostics are retained separately from the log tail. Review the generated report before sharing it.

name: Dashboard dashboard-v0.20.1
body:
## Fixes

- **Broca sessions show their data again.** Newer Broca versions write session records with features this dashboard didn't recognise yet, so those sessions showed "no data". The dashboard now reads them.
- **Cache Diagnostics no longer blames a pass that changed nothing.** A Magic Context pass that left the request unchanged was sometimes shown as the cause of a cache bust. Only passes that actually changed the request are named now. (#713)
- **Cache Diagnostics labels cache losses Magic Context didn't cause.** It now shows "Cache expired after N min idle" when the gap since the previous request was longer than the cache lifetime. It shows "Provider cache miss (no change recorded by Magic Context)" when a warm cache went cold seconds later and Magic Context recorded no change to the request. When the cache lifetime isn't known and the gap falls between the provider's shortest and longest lifetimes, the bust stays unlabelled, because either cause is possible. A cause Magic Context recorded always takes precedence. (#713)

name: v0.49.7
body:
# v0.49.7

This patch release reduces pauses during background work, makes image cleanup work across providers, and fixes conversation replay on OpenCode, Pi and Oh My Pi. There is no database migration.

## Upgrading

- **No migration.** `context.db` stays at schema 95 and `store.db` at schema 63. Restart OpenCode 1, OpenCode 2, Pi or Oh My Pi after updating.
- **Rust mode needs an updated `ck-mc`.** Update Magic Context's Rust module executable (`ck-mc`) as well as the plugin to receive the Rust image-cleanup and raw-replay fixes. Updating the plugin alone does not update `ck-mc`.

## Fixed

- **OpenCode no longer pauses for several seconds while Magic Context updates a compaction marker.** The marker's database connection no longer takes on OpenCode's pending WAL checkpoint work. Marker updates still wait for their database write to succeed before being used.
- **Pi and Oh My Pi stay responsive while background memory tasks read old sessions.** Historical scans and primer assembly now yield between bounded chunks instead of occupying the main thread for the whole scan. Memory-candidate searches also run asynchronously.
- **Background memory mapping finishes its work instead of timing out.** Batches now fit within their step budget and keep every mapping they found even if a batch stops early, so the dreamer no longer reports a slow model when the batch was simply too large. This applies on every host.
- **Old processed images are cleaned up on every provider, not just Anthropic.** This includes tool-result images and OpenCode 2's native media parts. Recent images remain protected, including images without their own message tag; an image whose position cannot be established is kept. Saved cleanup decisions replay consistently after a restart or a provider change (issue 699).
- **Rust-mode image cleanup no longer leaves mismatched thinking or image parts behind.** Some providers sign a model's thinking blocks and reject requests if the surrounding history becomes inconsistent. Cleanup now handles those blocks, image placeholders and tool-result images together and replays saved decisions consistently. Rust mode follows the same recent-image protection rule as OpenCode and Pi (issue 699).
- **Sticky notes no longer move relative to saved search hints on later turns.** First delivery and subsequent replays use the same position, avoiding an unnecessary prompt-cache change. A note that must wait for a safe history rewrite is not treated as delivered merely because a rewrite was allowed.
- **A retry after a partially saved reduction keeps the reductions that were saved.** Pi and OpenCode reconcile the last successfully sent request with committed drop decisions instead of bringing already-dropped content back into the retry. A retry is refused if those changes would invalidate retained signed thinking. Split tool results remain bound to the correct tool call, and ambiguous older tool identities are left untouched. Pi also saves stale context-tool cleanup before changing the outgoing history.
- **Oh My Pi correctly rewrites native assistant text after it is dropped or compressed.** Replies represented as `output_text` now reflect the managed history instead of retaining their original text. This continues the compatibility fixes prompted by the reports in issues 686 and 698; thanks @Qiiks.
- **Pi stops repeatedly retrying compaction markers whose synthetic anchor has been absorbed into a real user message.** Those unusable markers are diagnosed and retired; markers that can still be recovered remain eligible for retry (issue 693).
- **Search results can be expanded even when the host no longer exposes the original message.** When retained search-index text is available, `ctx_expand` returns that text and identifies it as an archive excerpt rather than claiming to return the complete original conversation. This also covers Pi results from history that is no longer on the active branch.
- **Rust-mode replay stays stable when message tags arrive late.** Content already sent during streaming is not rewritten just because a later pass can assign it a tag. When previously sent source content changes or disappears, recovery is bounded instead of repeatedly refusing the same history, and replay evidence no longer stores another full copy of large tool outputs.
- **Slow database writes are easier to diagnose.** Writes that wait for or hold the context database writer for more than 100 ms are attributed in the logs. Pi prepares saved-request metadata before acquiring the writer, reducing the time other sessions have to wait.

name: v0.49.6
body:
# v0.49.6

This patch release stops turns from being interrupted when Magic Context's database is briefly busy. There is no database migration.

## Upgrading

- **No migration.** `context.db` stays at schema 95 and `store.db` at schema 63. Restart OpenCode 1, OpenCode 2, Pi or Oh My Pi after updating.

## Fixed

- **Turns are no longer interrupted when the database is briefly busy.** Magic Context saves each turn's state before the request is sent. When another process (another OpenCode or Pi window, the dashboard, or a background task) was writing at the same moment, a turn waited only 250 ms for the database. If it couldn't safely reuse the last request it sent, it stopped the turn, and the session showed "Interrupted" with no reason. A turn now waits up to 2 seconds before giving up. Magic Context still never sends a session's history unmanaged: if the database stays busy longer, it reuses the last request it sent when that is safe, and otherwise stops the turn as before. [`60206b50ed`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/60206b50ed).

name: v0.49.5
body:
# v0.49.5

This patch release fixes two more cases where Oh My Pi turns failed with "provider request does not match this pass's managed dispatch". It also stops a harmless error from appearing in the Oh My Pi log. There is no database migration.

## Upgrading

- **No migration.** `context.db` stays at schema 95 and `store.db` at schema 63. Restart OpenCode 1, OpenCode 2, Pi or Oh My Pi after updating.

## Fixed

### Oh My Pi

- **Sessions with many images no longer fail.** To stay within a provider's image limit, Oh My Pi leaves the oldest images out of each request (it keeps five when the provider has no limit of its own). Magic Context's check now expects this: only the oldest images may be missing, in order, and everything else must still match. Sessions with fewer images are checked exactly as before (#686, thanks @Qiiks). [`418f5b8f42`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/418f5b8f42).
- **Sessions that keep a tool result without its tool call no longer fail.** This can happen after a compaction summary. Oh My Pi sends such a result as a short note saying the tool result is stale, and Magic Context's check now expects the same note. A tool result whose call is still in the history must match exactly (#698). [`f1b167faf1`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/f1b167faf1).
- **"Pi context pass superseded" no longer appears in the log.** It was logged when a newer turn replaced an older one before the older one had finished saving. Nothing was lost. Other errors of this kind are still logged (#698). [`636394d0df`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/636394d0df).

Tested with Oh My Pi 18.10.4, 18.11.0 and 18.11.1.

name: v0.49.4
body:
# v0.49.4

This patch release fixes Oh My Pi turns that 0.49.3 still refused with "provider request does not match this pass's managed dispatch", and makes every failed history summary record why it failed. There is no database migration.

## Upgrading

- **No migration.** `context.db` stays at schema 95 and `store.db` at schema 63. Restart OpenCode 1, OpenCode 2, Pi or Oh My Pi after updating.

## Fixed

### Oh My Pi

- **Sessions with extension messages or a compaction summary are no longer refused on the chat-completions API.** The check now builds those rows the way Oh My Pi does: custom extension messages and compaction summaries become user rows, and only rows left with no text or images are dropped (#686, thanks @Qiiks). [`4e0619d73b`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/4e0619d73b).
- **Sessions with earlier replies from other models are no longer refused on the Responses and Codex APIs.** The check now models those replies the way Oh My Pi sends them. When a reply can't be modelled, it no longer compares against a shape that could never match; it still refuses any request that doesn't carry Magic Context's prepared history (#686, thanks @Qiiks). [`4e0619d73b`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/4e0619d73b).

### History

- **Every failed history summary now records a reason.** On Pi and Oh My Pi a failed run used to store an empty reason. Magic Context's own reasons are kept word for word; provider and other external errors keep their status, error type and code, with no provider text; a Pi subprocess failure keeps its exit code and the first line of a known launch error, such as an extension that failed to load (#694). [`72d298a84d`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/72d298a84d).

name: v0.49.3
body:
# v0.49.3
