This patch release fixes more Oh My Pi turns refused with "provider request does not match this pass's managed dispatch", repairs Pi and Oh My Pi history after `/tree` navigation, keeps headless SDK subagents within their context window, and stops a summarizing chunk from leaving out a trailing tool result. There is no database migration.

## Upgrading

- **No migration.** `context.db` stays at schema 95 and `store.db` at schema 63. Restart OpenCode 1, OpenCode 2, Pi or Oh My Pi after updating.
- **Rust transform mode:** update `ck-mc` too, then restart the host and module.
- **One-time cache rewrites.** An Oh My Pi session on a Responses, Codex or Anthropic API that is currently refused because of an old dropped tool result rewrites the prompt cache once when the result is removed. On chat-completions APIs the removal waits for a cache rewrite that was already due. A Pi or Oh My Pi session that `/tree` moved back into summarized history rebuilds once to drop the abandoned summaries.

## Fixed

### Oh My Pi

- **Assistant replies with thinking from the same model are no longer refused on the Responses and Codex APIs.** The request carries that thinking as reasoning items, not text, and the check now groups those replies the same way (#686). [`80f03c538e`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/80f03c538e).
- **Oh My Pi advisor requests on OpenAI-style models are no longer refused.** The check now recognises the advisor's instruction and tool layout on chat-completions, Responses and Codex as well as Anthropic; main requests are still checked (#686, thanks @Qiiks). [`2a12a780d0`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/2a12a780d0).
- **A user profile, project memory or project docs block containing text that Oh My Pi masks, such as something that looks like a secret, no longer causes a refusal.** Magic Context now recognises its own blocks by their opening markers, which Oh My Pi does not change (#686). [`52e0577064`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/52e0577064).
- **Native `/fork`, branch and `/btw` copies keep Magic Context's tag history and summaries** from the session they were copied from, so their next turn is not refused. Stock Pi forks behave as before (#686). [`8afdf85a48`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/8afdf85a48).
- **Sessions whose history passed through OpenAI or Codex automatic compaction, or that were imported from the Codex CLI, are no longer refused on every turn.** Oh My Pi stores a copy of the compacted history on the summary message and, when it builds the request, uses that copy in place of everything before it, which also hid Magic Context's own history. Magic Context now sends the summary without that copy, so Oh My Pi uses the readable summary text. The copy stays in the session file, and assistant replies are not touched (#692). [`8e98e1ab08`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/8e98e1ab08).
- **Switching an Oh My Pi session to another provider API mid-conversation no longer causes a refusal.** Tool calls made on the Responses API carry combined ids, and Oh My Pi shortens them differently on each API; the check now applies Oh My Pi's own id rule for the request's actual API instead of guessing the API from the request's shape (#686, thanks @Qiiks). [`6cbd037228`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/6cbd037228).
- **A tool call left without a result, such as after an interrupted turn, no longer causes a refusal.** Oh My Pi fills in a placeholder result for it ("No result provided", or "aborted"), and the check now expects that placeholder; any other extra result is still refused (#686, thanks @Qiiks). [`e14688396f`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/e14688396f).
- **Old dropped tool results whose call is gone are removed instead of being sent as stale user notes.** Oh My Pi turned such results into user messages, which the check refused; they are now removed once and stay removed across restarts (#686, thanks @Qiiks). [`708f752e50`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/708f752e50), [`f343e401f6`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/f343e401f6).

### Pi and Oh My Pi

- **`/tree` back into summarized history no longer keeps summaries from the abandoned branch.** They are removed from the first point that is no longer on the active branch, the history that remains is summarized again, and `/ctx-wrapup` can make progress (#562). [`b79a5c88ce`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/b79a5c88ce), [`0cd814bbcb`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/0cd814bbcb).
- **Headless SDK subagents now summarize their history and stay within the model's window.** The historian runs in the background during headless runs. A request proven larger than the window waits for it, reclaims space, and is refused locally if it still does not fit, instead of being sent oversized. Uncertain size estimates never refuse a request or cause an extra cache rewrite (#689). [`25c73a7942`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/25c73a7942), [`b93f12ae33`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/b93f12ae33), [`0640e9aaa4`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/0640e9aaa4).
- **When a native compaction marker has to wait, the log says why, once per marker**, and the startup line names the sessions with a waiting marker (#693). [`95b9a745fa`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/95b9a745fa), [`9bc3fc4529`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/9bc3fc4529).

### History

- **OpenCode 1 and 2 (including Rust mode), Pi and Oh My Pi: a tool result at the end of a summarizing chunk stays inside that chunk.** When the result was shown together with its call (as the built-in `historian.expand_tools` templates do for todo updates), the chunk stopped at the call, so the historian's summary was rejected with "Historian terminal boundary splits a completed tool invocation/result arc". Trailing reminders and other filtered rows now count toward the chunk as well; the text sent to the historian is unchanged (#690). [`fae2cde60d`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/fae2cde60d).

name: v0.49.2
body:
# v0.49.2

This patch release fixes Oh My Pi turns refused by a check that 0.49.1 added: in sessions with history, on the Responses API, and with several other provider APIs, every turn could be refused with "provider request does not match this pass's managed dispatch (prepared turn structure)". Oh My Pi's `doctor --issue` report now includes recent errors and the log. There is no database migration.

## Upgrading

- **No migration.** `context.db` stays at schema 95 and `store.db` at schema 63. Restart Oh My Pi after updating.
- **Only Pi, Oh My Pi and the CLI change.** OpenCode 1 and 2 behave exactly as in 0.49.1.

## Fixed

### Oh My Pi

- **Sessions whose input starts with a system entry are no longer refused on every turn.** The check that compares the outgoing request with the prepared turn skipped leading system and developer entries on the request side but rejected them on the prepared side. Both sides now skip them the same way; a system entry later in the conversation is still refused (#686, #683, thanks @Qiiks). [`d3b0cbdf1c`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/d3b0cbdf1c).
- **Sessions with runs of consecutive assistant messages are no longer refused on the Responses API**, for example commentary text followed by an answer from cached Responses history. The check merged those messages into one row on the request side but kept them separate on the prepared side; both sides now group them the same way and compare every text item (#686, thanks @Qiiks). [`bde7c878ff`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/bde7c878ff).
- **Turns with older history are no longer refused on the chat-completions API** (including Cline models). The check now recognises what Oh My Pi's converter does to that history: it drops empty and reasoning-only assistant replies, moves tool-result images into their own message, and turns a tool result whose call is missing into a note (#683). [`04ed01228d`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/04ed01228d).
- **Requests are no longer refused on the Google, Vertex, Gemini CLI, Bedrock and Azure Responses APIs, or on Ollama with tool history.** The check now reads each of these APIs' native request shape (#683). [`593c73a50b`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/593c73a50b), [`c45f1e0d8b`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/c45f1e0d8b).
- **A refusal from this check now says where the request differed**: the first differing message position, message counts, roles and which comparison failed. It never includes message text, tool names or ids. [`2675e58aeb`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/2675e58aeb).

Requests that Magic Context did not prepare are still refused, as in 0.49.1.

### CLI

- **Oh My Pi `doctor --issue` reports include environment details, the last 20 errors and the last 400 log lines**, sanitized and capped to GitHub's issue size like the Pi and OpenCode reports. Magic Context turn refusals now count as errors in these reports on every host, so a capped report keeps them. [`6bc0264962`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/6bc0264962).

name: v0.49.1
body:
# v0.49.1

This patch release fixes a memory leak in long Pi sessions, Oh My Pi turns refused after a late end notification, Pi exiting when Esc cancels a long tool call, and several avoidable prompt-cache rewrites after a flush or a busy database. It also makes the ONNX Runtime telemetry opt-out effective for local embeddings and adds a Restore action for dismissed user memories in the dashboard. There is no database migration.

## Upgrading

- **No migration.** `context.db` stays at schema 95 and `store.db` at schema 63. Restart OpenCode 1, OpenCode 2, Pi or Oh My Pi after updating.
- **OpenCode 2 needs an explicit plugin update.** Use `/plugins` and ctrl+u, or `opencode plugin update`; refreshing the plugin list does not install updates. [Details](https://docs.cortexkit.io/magic-context/getting-started/opencode-2/#updating-magic-context-on-opencode-2).
- **Rust transform mode:** update `ck-mc` too, then restart the host and module.
- **Dashboard changes require an updated dashboard build.** The desktop app has its own [releases](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/releases?q=dashboard&expanded=true).
- **`models.window_overlay_path` is deprecated and ignored.** Fusiform no longer publishes window-overlay data, so removing the setting changes nothing in practice. Configs that still set it load normally with a deprecation warning; remove the key.

## New

- **Dashboard: dismissed user memories can be restored to the active set** with a Restore button, and running sessions pick up the restored entry (#670, thanks @ICEY16360). [`c936fa7567`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/c936fa7567), [`1d609401eb`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/1d609401eb).

## Changed

- **OpenCode 1 and 2 (including Rust mode), Pi and Oh My Pi: `ctx_reduce` replies with a short count**, such as "3 tags stamped.", instead of listing each queued or held tag. [`ba021fdcc9`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/ba021fdcc9), [`a630c7cb62`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/a630c7cb62).
- **OpenCode 1 and 2, Pi and Oh My Pi: after a busy database forced Magic Context to serve a saved request, that request is not resent after a restart until a normal pass has rebuilt it.** If the database is still busy on the first turn after the restart, that turn is refused instead of sending an out-of-date request; the next turn with the database free rebuilds normally. Windows cannot record this across a restart, so there a request saved during busy-database recovery is never resent after a restart. [`eadcb52a5a`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/eadcb52a5a), [`cc47f005bb`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/cc47f005bb).

## Fixed

### Oh My Pi

- **Turns are no longer refused when the previous run's end notification arrives after the context was published or in the middle of a run**, including goal continuations and provider fallback retries (#673, #674, thanks @Qiiks). [`1dce69accf`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/1dce69accf), [`4d7ecc0f61`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/4d7ecc0f61), [`06f89f99ea`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/06f89f99ea).
- **The first chat-completions request in headless mode is no longer refused** because of the system instruction Oh My Pi adds itself (#673, thanks @Qiiks). [`7a21d17ffd`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/7a21d17ffd).

### Pi

- **Pressing Esc during a long tool call cancels the call instead of exiting Pi** (#680, thanks @luelueluez7Z). [`11c4f12401`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/11c4f12401).
- **`pi.subagent_extensions` passes `npm:`, `git:`, `github:`, `http:`, `https:`, `ssh:` and `builtin:` sources through to Pi** instead of resolving them as relative paths; `~` and `file://` entries are expanded (#677, thanks @Shrub24). [`7cd7bc2c02`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/7cd7bc2c02).
- **Pi and Oh My Pi: an old system reminder that was already removed no longer reappears during Claude thinking tool calls and disappears again on the next user message**, which rewrote the prompt cache each time. [`caa7db3415`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/caa7db3415).

### OpenCode 2

- **Tag notation the model copied into its own replies is no longer sent back to it** on later requests; the stored reply is unchanged (#671, thanks @CaptKitCarson). [`7eca5261d4`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/7eca5261d4).

### OpenCode 1 and 2 in Rust mode

- **`/ctx-flush` on a session that has no summarized history yet now takes effect** instead of staying queued. [`320ab695ae`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/320ab695ae).

### Prompt cache

- **OpenCode 1 and 2, Pi and Oh My Pi: Claude thinking signatures are no longer counted as text**, which could trigger a false 95% context emergency and an unneeded rebuild. [`9b347d26d1`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/9b347d26d1).
- **OpenCode 1 and 2: after a rebuild, the next request trims history at the same point the rebuilt request used**, instead of cutting differently and rewriting the cache again. [`9b347d26d1`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/9b347d26d1), [`baaebec0f3`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/baaebec0f3).
- **OpenCode 1 and 2 (including Rust mode): the date in the system prompt's environment block no longer rewrites the cache at midnight**; it updates with the next prompt rebuild, and only for the request that is rebuilding. [`9b347d26d1`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/9b347d26d1), [`e1f75688af`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/e1f75688af).
- **OpenCode 1 and 2: an image strip that fails to save is no longer applied**, so the image is not removed on one pass and sent again on the next. [`6320a8b418`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/6320a8b418).
- **OpenCode 1 and 2 (including Rust mode), Pi and Oh My Pi: a system-prompt change during a Claude thinking turn no longer causes a second rebuild on the next wake.** [`fdd2c3674f`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/fdd2c3674f), [`fd258448fd`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/fd258448fd).
- **OpenCode 1 and 2, Pi and Oh My Pi: after a busy database forces a saved request to be served, later passes no longer add tags to messages already sent**, avoiding a cache rewrite. [`eadcb52a5a`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/eadcb52a5a), [`cc47f005bb`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/cc47f005bb), [`7bb0871a73`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/7bb0871a73).

### Local embeddings

- **OpenCode 1 and 2, Pi and Oh My Pi: the ONNX Runtime telemetry opt-out now takes effect for local embeddings under Bun and Node**, including compiled Bun hosts. On Windows, ONNX Runtime uses the operating system's event tracing instead, and a one-time log line explains this (#672, thanks @botbeech). [`ecb17b4b23`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/ecb17b4b23), [`a51d353793`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/a51d353793).

### Pi memory

- **Pi and Oh My Pi: a long session no longer keeps every completed context pass in memory.** Each pass's ownership check held on to the previous pass and its full message history, so memory grew with every turn until the session was cleared, reaching several gigabytes in long native Pi sessions. Completed passes are now released after each turn (#681, thanks @chpock). [`d42b7c801d`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/d42b7c801d).

## Security

- **Smart-note file conditions refuse symbolic links whose target does not exist**, rather than evaluating a path that could later point elsewhere. [`5950150519`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/5950150519).

name: v0.49.0
body:
# v0.49.0

This release stops repeated prompt-cache rewrites during Claude thinking and tool loops, reduces delays in long sessions, and addresses Oh My Pi turns blocked by late context notifications or sending history without context preparation. It also corrects historian settings and reporting. There is no database migration.

## Upgrading

- **No migration.** `context.db` stays at schema 95. Restart OpenCode 1, OpenCode 2, Pi or Oh My Pi after updating.
- **OpenCode 2 needs an explicit plugin update.** Use `/plugins` and ctrl+u, or `opencode plugin update`; refreshing the plugin list does not install updates. [Details](https://docs.cortexkit.io/magic-context/getting-started/opencode-2/#updating-magic-context-on-opencode-2).
- **Rust transform mode:** update `ck-mc` too, then restart the host and module.
- **Dashboard changes require an updated dashboard build.** The desktop app has its own [releases](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/releases?q=dashboard&expanded=true).
- **No new configuration keys or changed defaults.** Existing historian model, variant, temperature, timeout and output-limit settings remain in use.

## New

- **OpenCode 1 and 2, Pi and Oh My Pi: `ctx_search` uses Synapse's ranking service to reorder results for natural-language queries when available.** Short symbol or path lookups and automatic search hints keep the previous ranking; unavailable or failed reranking also falls back unchanged. Installs without Synapse keep exactly the previous results. [`a87b65cb07`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/a87b65cb07).

## Changed

- **OpenCode 1 and 2, Pi and Oh My Pi: background-model temperature is sent only when model metadata explicitly supports it**, using the cached models.dev catalogue when host metadata is silent; unknown support omits the parameter. [`cdd3dedf7f`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/cdd3dedf7f), [`5a76f22fea`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/5a76f22fea), [`7e90bdc95f`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/7e90bdc95f).
- **OpenCode 1 and 2 in Rust mode: historian and dreamer transcripts request up to one day's retention where the model runner supports it**; older runners keep their own lifetime policy. [`6b780869c2`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/6b780869c2).

### Performance

- **Pi and Oh My Pi: faster turn preparation in long sessions**, reusing previously checked message identities and tags instead of repeatedly scanning the full history. [`873ee68257`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/873ee68257), [`76ecddcf7b`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/76ecddcf7b), [`edb6de0758`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/edb6de0758), [`4a88f90f6b`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/4a88f90f6b).
- **OpenCode 1 and 2: fewer main-thread stalls while resolving summary boundaries and reading history after a restart.** [`1a34bc5316`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/1a34bc5316), [`61fe94608d`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/61fe94608d).
- **OpenCode 1 and 2, Pi and Oh My Pi: `ctx_reduce` checks only the requested tags**, avoiding a full-session scan for each call. [`1a34bc5316`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/1a34bc5316).
- **OpenCode 1 and 2 in Rust mode: faster context preparation in large sessions**, with fewer repeated history scans and token counts while preserving the same model requests. [`4f33ce6e55`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/4f33ce6e55), [`4604f276fb`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/4604f276fb), [`468a873aad`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/468a873aad).

## Fixed

### OpenCode 2

- **`/btw` reuses the latest prepared system prompt, history and tool definitions even after tool results without message IDs**, preserving the new side question instead of using history from an earlier main request (#666). [`7b3766c9c7`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/7b3766c9c7).
- **On Windows, scheduled dreamer tasks run again.** Session directories stored with forward slashes now match the plugin's backslash paths, so timer-started runs find their session; sessions from other folders are still kept out (#669). [`e3617d9049`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/e3617d9049).
- **Configured historian temperature now reaches historian, editor and recompression requests when the selected model supports it.** [`96cd2dec6a`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/96cd2dec6a).

### OpenCode 1 and 2, Pi and Oh My Pi

- **Unfinished Claude thinking and tool loops no longer rewrite earlier history mid-turn.** Queued cleanup, including `/ctx-flush`, waits and lands once in a single rebuild after the turn; when a rewrite cannot wait, the provider-signed thinking that depends on the old history is removed first (#665). [`f11f9737db`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/f11f9737db), [`c49b1526bf`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/c49b1526bf).
- **The log names the real reason a turn's cleanup is held**, once per turn, instead of reporting an unresolved session directory (#664). [`c49b1526bf`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/c49b1526bf).

### Pi and Oh My Pi

- **Tag and history caches are refreshed correctly after session clears, message replacements or reuse of a deleted session ID**, preventing stale message associations. [`00a1d29944`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/00a1d29944), [`f01bba51d8`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/f01bba51d8).
- **The historian recognizes newly tagged history after the first local tags are created**, instead of continuing to read an empty cached view. [`784bdd8ead`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/784bdd8ead).
- **Fallback message matching detects tag writes from older builds**, including when another process writes the same session. [`c2a707dc99`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/c2a707dc99), [`43f8057a2b`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/43f8057a2b).
- **Completed context passes keep their diagnostic decision rows even when the next pass starts more than 25 seconds later.** [`7ed16a4e87`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/7ed16a4e87).

### Oh My Pi

- **A replaced context pass no longer causes a false refusal of the newer prepared turn**, including when the previous turn's end notification arrives late (#667). [`d226af895a`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/d226af895a), [`cda226f5a5`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/cda226f5a5), [`e420907676`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/e420907676).
- **Unreadable input message lists produce a visible context refusal rather than letting an error escape the context hook** (#667). [`d310f34c66`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/d310f34c66).
- **Refusal diagnostics distinguish an ended turn from missing preparation and identify the last preparation stage**, instead of incorrectly reporting a database write failure (#663). [`a1415d7fbf`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/a1415d7fbf), [`f6a40f5700`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/f6a40f5700).
- **Stale, unprepared requests from recently replaced context passes are rejected**, rather than accepted using the newer pass's preparation (#668). [`2144ebb366`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/2144ebb366), [`850a28cbde`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/850a28cbde), [`cf68110a93`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/cf68110a93).
- **`/dump` on Oh My Pi 18.10.3 no longer runs context preparation or changes the live turn's preparation state** (#668). [`850a28cbde`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/850a28cbde).
- **Ordinary provider sends avoid serializing the entire conversation when there are no rejected stale requests to check** (#668). [`cf68110a93`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/cf68110a93).

### OpenCode 1 and 2 in Rust mode

- **Unfinished Anthropic thinking/tool loops keep the history preceding signed reasoning unchanged**, including after prompt-cache expiry; a necessary history rewrite or context-limit recovery removes the signed reasoning first, and a request that still cannot fit is refused (#665). [`b554fea74c`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/b554fea74c), [`3c57193092`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/3c57193092), [`d2814a4209`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/d2814a4209), [`4c99df8733`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/4c99df8733).
- **`/ctx-wrapup` uses the current historian model chain, variants, timeout and output cap**, even when earlier context passes have failed. [`7b31d27f31`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/7b31d27f31), [`60bdfd333a`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/60bdfd333a).
- **Historian attempts honor each model's configured variant**, including fallback models. [`fd26673701`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/fd26673701).
- **A still-running context transform reports that the engine is busy rather than immediately treating it as disconnected**, and does not send unprepared history while that transform may still complete. [`cc91e31aca`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/cc91e31aca), [`60bdfd333a`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/60bdfd333a).
- **Historian attempts can restart when their retained transcript has expired**, rather than treating missing history as a model failure. [`6b780869c2`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/6b780869c2).
- **Cache diagnostics attribute the history rewrite when a saved recovery request is replaced by newly prepared context.** [`6309150a1a`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/6309150a1a).

### Dashboard and status

- **OpenCode 1 and 2 in Rust mode: historian runs appear again in the dashboard and `/ctx-status`**, with model attempts, fallback relationships, errors, usage and published-output metrics recorded without blocking the run. [`bba149fca4`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/bba149fca4).

### Shared fixes

- **OpenCode 1 and 2, Pi and Oh My Pi: automatic search hints stay unchanged across search failures, retries and branch switches**, avoiding late edits to messages already sent to the model. [`d4f5412c61`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/d4f5412c61), [`6c162642ac`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/6c162642ac), [`f906923e56`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/f906923e56).
- **OpenCode 1 and 2, Pi and Oh My Pi: a busy database while saving an automatic-search decision no longer refuses the turn**; it serves without a hint and retries saving that decision later. [`43ddbe1bec`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/43ddbe1bec).
- **OpenCode 1 and 2: screenshot-heavy sessions can save larger recovery requests**, avoiding repeated refusals caused by the previous snapshot-size limit. [`b0b8628bca`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/b0b8628bca).
- **OpenCode 1 and 2, Pi and Oh My Pi: concurrent log writers no longer rotate the same log twice and overwrite the previous log.** [`66873d6d04`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/commit/66873d6d04).

name: v0.48.0
body:
# v0.48.0

This release reduces pauses in large sessions and fixes turns that could get stuck on OpenCode, Pi and Oh My Pi. It adds a switch for smart notes, extends the stall profiler to Pi and Oh My Pi, and updates the dashboard and doctor. There is no database migration.

## Upgrading

- **No migration.** `context.db` stays at schema 95. Restart OpenCode 1, OpenCode 2, Pi or Oh My Pi after updating.
- **OpenCode 2 needs an explicit plugin update.** Use `/plugins` and ctrl+u, or `opencode plugin update`; refreshing the plugin list does not install updates. [Details](https://docs.cortexkit.io/magic-context/getting-started/opencode-2/#updating-magic-context-on-opencode-2).
- **Rust transform mode:** update `ck-mc` too, then restart the host and module.
- **`mural.model` is deprecated and ignored**, including `experimental.mural.model`. Use `dreamer.<harness>.tasks.compress-cues.model`, where `<harness>` is `opencode`, `pi` or `omp`. [Details](https://docs.cortexkit.io/magic-context/concepts/mural/#compress-cues-dreamer-task).
- **Changing `smart_notes.enabled` requires a restart.** Set it only in user config, not project config. The default remains `true`. [Details](https://docs.cortexkit.io/magic-context/reference/tools/#ctx_note).
- **Dashboard changes require an updated dashboard build.** The desktop app has its own [releases](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/releases?q=dashboard&expanded=true).

## New

- **Smart notes can be disabled:** `smart_notes.enabled: false` stops condition-based authoring and evaluation. Ordinary notes and already-ready notes remain available. [Details](https://docs.cortexkit.io/magic-context/reference/tools/#ctx_note).
- **Pi and Oh My Pi: the optional host stall profiler records stalls** while `<storage>/host-profiler/enable` exists; remove it to stop. [Details](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/blob/master/docs/reports/host-stall-profiler.md).
- **OpenCode 2: experimental transcript compaction reduces long-session delays without changing model requests.** Off by default; launch with `MC_OC2_INVISIBLE_FOLD=1` (#632, thanks @moynzzz). [Details](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/blob/master/docs/reports/issue-632-memory-cache-fixes.md).
- **`magic-context doctor --verbose` prints the full dangling-compartment listing.** Ordinary output shows counts and up to ten examples.
- **Dashboard: edit `protected_tools` as named rows** with defaults and inline validation, instead of editing a JSON field.

## Changed

- **`compress-cues` inherits the current host's dreamer model by default**, with an override in that host's task settings. The dashboard removes `mural.model`.
- **Magic Context no longer refuses turns because another machine claims the checkout**; the per-turn check is removed and MC-C16 is retired.

### Performance

- **OpenCode 1 and 2:** less waiting while counting history and checking reasoning in large sessions, including the first turn after a restart.
- **OpenCode 1 and 2:** fewer UI stalls during `ctx_search` message-history searches and search-index updates.
- **OpenCode 1 and 2:** history counts remain available as new messages arrive, avoiding repeated warm-up delays in long sessions.
- **Pi and Oh My Pi:** faster turn preparation and old-reasoning cleanup in long sessions.

### Dashboard

- **Historian rows show the provider and fallback attempts**, and errors appear as a red icon with details on hover instead of widening the table.
- **Pi session pages show compartment dates.** Session headers and background-model tabs are aligned more consistently.
- **Model discovery uses a corner notification**, so loading OpenCode models no longer moves the configuration page around.

## Fixed

### OpenCode 1

- **Saving the last good request no longer freezes OpenCode on large tool metadata the model never sees** (#653, thanks @maxbrunet).
- **Startup fallback respects `OPENCODE_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG`**, instead of disabling Magic Context because of native-compaction settings in an ignored project config.

### OpenCode 2

- **Anthropic requests no longer contain empty text left by context cleanup**, preventing repeated HTTP 400 errors; prompt-cache hints are preserved (#662, thanks @moynzzz).
- **`/ctx-*` commands appear once in the command palette**, and status, progress and completion feedback are restored (#661, thanks @JKratto).

### Pi

- **Other extensions' system-prompt sections reach the model**, even when those extensions load after Magic Context (#648, #649, thanks @st0nie).
- **Pi/Oh My Pi: conflicting `@msg` and `@tool` references no longer permanently block a session as “storage busy”** (#650, thanks @bin115885).
- **Pi/Oh My Pi: the historian can continue after early session entries go missing**, provided saved history identifies the remaining messages.
- **Pi/Oh My Pi: `ctx_expand` reports “no longer in history”** for messages the host no longer retains.
- **Pi/Oh My Pi: `/ctx-wrapup` no longer leaves a resolvable compaction marker waiting indefinitely** (#652, marker anchoring only, thanks @acamq).
- **Pi/Oh My Pi: auto-search skips system notices and steer messages**, rather than treating them as new user requests.
- **Node's SQLite experimental warning no longer repeats at startup or in child sessions**; other warnings remain visible (#651, thanks @Zzz210s).
- **Pi/Oh My Pi: configured background models are not reported disabled before discovery finishes**, including during session or project changes (#656, #658, thanks @randomvariable).

### Oh My Pi

- **Compiled Oh My Pi: dreamer loads the host session API**, and token counting finds plugin-installed dependencies (#655, #657, thanks @randomvariable).
- **Old messages can still be removed after Oh My Pi compacts its transcript**, preventing long sessions from exceeding the context window again.
- **Delayed turn starts no longer cause false “missing managed context receipt” refusals**, and advisor reviews can run (#663, thanks @Qiiks).

### CLI and doctor

- **Hosts without a Magic Context registration show INFO rather than FAIL**; `doctor --force` does not install Magic Context there.
- **Doctor ignores unused cached plugin copies when checking active installations**, reports them as INFO and leaves them untouched.

### Shared fixes

- **OpenCode 1 and 2: historian scheduling recovers after history-index updates**, instead of silently staying idle.
- **Dreamer keeps checking a memory batch when one proposed edit duplicates another memory**, instead of failing the batch, in TypeScript and Rust modes.
- **Recovery from a busy database no longer fails when a fresh [memory mural](https://docs.cortexkit.io/magic-context/concepts/mural/) is needed** on OpenCode, Pi or Oh My Pi.
- **Closing a Bun SQLite connection releases its database locks**, even after its statements have been garbage-collected.

## Security

- **Dashboard:** TLS dependencies are updated to rustls 0.23.45 and rustls-webpki 0.103.15.

name: Dashboard dashboard-v0.20.0
body:
## Dashboard v0.20.0

A light theme, a redesigned Cache page, and a faster, quieter app. Works with Magic Context 0.47.x.

### Light theme
The dashboard now has a light theme. A new picker in the sidebar offers System, Light and Dark; System is the default and follows your operating system. The light palette is a warm off-white rather than bright white, and all colours keep readable contrast in both themes. The chosen theme applies before the window paints, so there is no flash of the wrong theme on start.

### A redesigned Cache page
- Session cards show readable names instead of raw ids, and no longer repeat the same badges on every card.
- The timeline is drawn to scale against the model's context window, with a fill bar showing how full each request was.
- Turns are a table instead of raw text rows, and each fact appears once.
- Broca runs are measured against each run's own context window, and runs that were paused by a restart keep their later steps.

### Lighter on your machine
- The Cache page's Live mode reads only what changed since the last refresh instead of rescanning OpenCode's database and Broca's logs on every poll. With the Broca filter selected, a refresh went from about 627 ms and 454 MB read to under 5 ms.
- The Logs view stops refreshing while the window is hidden, slows down when it is not focused, and re-reads only log files that changed.

### Config page
- **Protected tools** is a small table of tools and how many of their newest results to keep, instead of a JSON box. The built-in defaults (the newest todo list and the newest three `ctx_reduce` calls) are shown, and an example explains the setting.
- **Keep reasoning tokens** replaces the old reasoning-age setting, matching Magic Context 0.47.0.
- **The cue compressor model** is no longer a separate shared field. Magic Context now picks it from each host's dreamer settings, like every other dreamer task; set a per-task model in the dreamer task table to override it. With Magic Context 0.47.x, an existing `mural.model` key still applies and can be edited in Raw JSONC.
- Session details show the number of historian runs instead of an "Execute hits" counter that always read 0.
- While models are loading, the status shows as a small notice in the corner instead of pushing the page down.

name: v0.47.0
body:
This minor release replaces the tag-age reasoning setting with a token budget, `keep_reasoning_tokens`, and stops Anthropic subagent tool loops being rejected after `ctx_reduce`. Pi and Oh My Pi (OMP) subagents survive a busy database, OMP's 30-second extension deadline can no longer send unmanaged history, and several Pi/OMP pressure readings that stopped the historian are fixed. Auto-search no longer holds up a turn. There is no database change.

## Upgrading

- **No migration.** The database stays at schema v95, so restarting OpenCode, OpenCode 2, Pi or OMP on 0.47.0 is enough.
- **`clear_reasoning_age` is replaced by `keep_reasoning_tokens`.** The old key is ignored with a warning. Run `magic-context doctor` to remove it; ages can't be converted to tokens, so doctor doesn't guess a value. Without a setting, every model now keeps a fixed 10,000 tokens of older reasoning.
- **OpenCode 2 still needs 2.0.22 or newer.** OpenCode 2 does not install plugin updates on its own: open `/plugins`, select Magic Context and press ctrl+u, or run `opencode plugin update`.
- **Rust transform mode (experimental): use the `ck-mc` from this release** to get the reasoning budget, the attachment fix and the Claude Haiku 5.5 thinking rules below.

## New

- **`keep_reasoning_tokens`: keep older reasoning by token count** (#620, requested by @tenshiak). Set a number, or a per-model map such as `{ "default": 10000, "openai/*": 6000 }`; `0` removes all older reasoning that can be removed. The newest reasoning is kept in whole steps until the budget runs out, and the newest step always stays. Removal only happens on passes that already rebuild the prompt cache. `/ctx-status` and the Pi status dialog show how much is kept. This applies on OpenCode 1 and 2, Pi, OMP and the Rust module. See the [configuration reference](https://docs.cortexkit.io/magic-context/reference/configuration/) and [context reduction](https://docs.cortexkit.io/magic-context/concepts/context-reduction/).
- **Host stall profiler (OpenCode 1, off by default).** When OpenCode's main thread stalls for several seconds, it writes a report naming the plugin whose code was running. Create `host-profiler/enable` in the Magic Context storage directory (`~/.local/share/cortexkit/magic-context` by default) to turn it on and delete it to turn it off, without a restart; reports appear in the same folder. Details: [`docs/reports/host-stall-profiler.md`](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/blob/master/docs/reports/host-stall-profiler.md).

## Changes

- **Status shows historian runs.** The Pi status dialog, Pi's `/ctx-status` details and the dashboard's session view now count recorded historian runs, in place of a threshold counter that always stayed at 0 (#634).
- **`/ctx-status` shows the context window it measures against:** the exact token count and where it came from, such as the provider's measurement or the model catalog (#634). This applies on OpenCode and Pi.
- **The historian sees room posts and private messages whole.** Historian input no longer cuts tool text at hidden limits, such as 400 characters for room posts. A `.truncate(N)` in `historian.expand_tools` now ends at a full sentence and says how much it left out.
- **Claude Haiku 5.5 gets the same signed-thinking handling as Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5,** so edits Anthropic would reject are held back. This applies on OpenCode, Pi and the Rust module.
- **Pi/OMP: the log records project binding changes and failed binding writes** (#646). When a session's project changes, for example after `/move`, the Magic Context log names the old and new project. A binding write that keeps failing is logged at most every 10 minutes, followed by one line when it recovers. Before, a failed write was retried silently.
- **OpenCode 2: a dreamer task stopped before its setup now says which one** (#647). The error names the task, the background session, its folder and the step that was missed, and notes that switching models won't help.
- **Rust transform mode: old images are cleared on the same schedule as in TypeScript mode,** no longer tied to reasoning age. An affected session makes this one-time change on its next cache rebuild.

## Fixes

- **Anthropic: a turn's thinking is no longer changed while the turn is still running** (#630, reported by @tppawelgrzesik). After `ctx_reduce`, a subagent's next request in the same tool loop could lose thinking blocks, and Anthropic rejected it ("thinking or redacted_thinking blocks in the latest assistant message cannot be modified"). Drops that would touch that thinking now wait until the next real user message. If a provider rejects a turn's thinking anyway and the host retries that turn, the retry sends the original blocks. This applies on OpenCode 1 and 2, Pi and the Rust module.
- **Pi/OMP: the historian is no longer blocked by an inflated window size** (#634, reported by @Zireael). A failed reply's usage could be saved as the model's measured capacity, so 834,000 input tokens read as 9.5% and the historian never started. Only successful provider readings count now, and inflated saved values are corrected from the session's history, on OpenCode too.
- **Pi: a pending compaction marker left behind after a history summary is expected** (#635, reported by @Zireael). It is cleared on the next pass that rebuilds the cache; the delay came from the deferrals fixed in #634, so no separate fix was needed.
- **OMP: per-turn billing usage is no longer read as context size** (#636, reported by @Zireael). Some OMP providers, such as Cursor, report a whole turn's usage on one message, which produced a phantom "2913%" emergency at real 94% usage. Readings larger than the model's window are now ignored and the request is measured instead.
- **Pi/OMP: a historian or subagent run keeps its finished reply** (#637, reported by @red-projects). An "aborted" event after the reply had finished could replace it, and the run failed with no result.
- **Dreamer: the retrospective task runs in SDK and bridge setups** (#638, reported by @salacoste). After its first run, sessions without host activity records counted as inactive, so scheduled runs were skipped forever. It now falls back to the session's message index.
- **Pi/OMP: a busy database no longer kills a subagent** (#640, reported by @TheOrdinaryWow). When another process held the database, the subagent's turn was refused and nothing resent it, so OMP cancelled the task. The turn now resends the last good request when it still fits, and otherwise waits up to about 16.5 seconds for the database. Two OMP-only mismatches that made a valid last good request look unusable are fixed, and a turn that is still refused says what it was waiting for. OpenCode 1 and 2 also try the last good request before waiting, and OpenCode 2 checks it against the current tools and system prompt.
- **OMP: the 30-second extension deadline can no longer send unmanaged history** (#641, reported by @Zireael). When Magic Context took longer than 30 seconds, OMP sent the raw conversation, and Magic Context then saved results the provider never saw. Context work now finishes within 25 seconds, and a request whose context work did not finish in time is stopped with a notice instead of being sent. On Pi and OMP, emergency cleanup no longer waits for a running historian. OMP side turns can't be told apart from main turns, so once a session has run a side turn, this dispatch check stays off for that session.
- **The historian no longer fails on a chunk that splits a tool call from its result** (#642, reported by @chpock). Under high pressure, the historian could be handed a single message that ended between a tool call and its result. No valid summary can end there, so every attempt failed with MC-H01 on every turn. Chunk selection now never cuts a tool call off from its result, and when no complete chunk exists the historian waits for one instead of failing. This applies on OpenCode and Pi.
- **OMP: `pi` historian and dreamer models are used** (#645, reported by @sisttri). Reloading config created an empty `omp` block that took priority over `pi`, so the historian and dreamer ran on OMP's default model.
- **Rust transform mode keeps tool-result attachments.** On OpenCode 1, images and PDFs from `read`, `computer_use` and other tools were dropped from tagged results. They are now sent, and results already sent without them get them back on the next cache rebuild. An attachment OpenCode can't represent shows an `[attachment not shown: …]` line instead of disappearing.

## Performance

- **Auto-search no longer holds up a turn.** The search runs in a separate read-only worker, and a turn waits at most 3 seconds for it; before, a 3-second limit could stretch to 5–7 seconds. A slow search, or one before the search index is ready after a start, skips the hint for that turn, and retries of that turn stay without it. This applies on OpenCode 1 and 2, Pi and OMP.
- **Less work when the historian's budget is spent.** When the historian has used its budget for the current 10-minute window, passes skip reading history and preparing its prompt, and the log says when it can run next. A historian run's startup work no longer runs inside the pass that schedules it. This applies on OpenCode and Pi.

## Internal

- `ARCHITECTURE.md` now states that an explicit `/ctx-flush` may apply queued drops while the historian runs; this was already the behavior.
- Investigation and review reports, design notes, profiling scripts and tests. CI builds the Pi package before plugin tests.

name: v0.46.1
body:
This patch release fixes a bug on OpenCode 2 where a background Magic Context agent could run outside its read-only setup and change files in another project. There is no database change in this release.

## Upgrading

- **No migration.** The database stays at schema v95, so restarting OpenCode or Pi on 0.46.1 is enough.
- **OpenCode 2 does not install plugin updates on its own:** open `/plugins`, select Magic Context and press ctrl+u, or run `opencode plugin update`.
- **If you're still on 0.46.0 with OpenCode 2,** keep the dreamer off (`"dreamer": { "disable": true }`, then restart OpenCode) or set your global `edit`, `write` and `shell` permissions to `ask` until you update.

## Fixes

- **OpenCode 2: background agents stay read-only and only run in their own project** (#639, reported by @sam-chainalysis). OpenCode 2 runs a separate copy of Magic Context for each project folder but tells every copy when a conversation finishes anywhere. The dreamer reacted to a conversation in another project and started its memory-mapping run there. That copy of Magic Context didn't recognise the run, so it was sent without its read-only instructions, and the user's own permissions applied because OpenCode checks them after a plugin agent's rules. In the report, the run edited infrastructure files. Five separate guards now prevent this, and each one stops it on its own:
  - the dreamer only reacts to conversations in its own folder;
  - a background session that ends up in another folder is removed before anything is sent;
  - Magic Context refuses any background-agent turn it didn't start, before the model is called;
  - each background session carries its own read-only rules, which OpenCode checks after yours;
  - any tool call outside a background agent's read-only list is refused, whatever your permissions say.

  The same cause explains the first-minute "Host did not dispatch the hidden child context hook" refusal after a restart (#602). OpenCode 1 and Pi were not affected.
- **`dreamer.disable` takes effect without a restart.** Scheduled runs, the turn-end trigger and `/ctx-dream` read it before each run, on OpenCode 1, OpenCode 2 and Pi.

## Performance

- **Faster compaction marker placement on long OpenCode 1 sessions.** Finding the user message where the marker goes made SQLite sort the whole session. On a 157,000-message session this took about 6 seconds of a turn. The lookup now walks back from the target and stops at the first match, with identical results.
- **The Pi status dialog does less work while open.** It rebuilds its detail every 10 seconds, or when the session or settings change, instead of every second, and caches its token estimates.

## Internal

- Test and CI changes that cut CPU use on shared machines: Pi tests run on four workers, CI runs each package suite once, the TUI is generated once per build, the Rust real-daemon tests build their daemon once, and the bundled SQLite in the Rust crates is built without its global memory counter.
- A live test harness for Anthropic signed-thinking edits, seeded from a recorded request.

name: v0.46.0
body:
This minor release adds `protected_tools`, which keeps the newest results of chosen tools out of every automatic drop, and turns smart drops on for everyone. It migrates the shared database to schema v95. In Rust transform mode on OpenCode 1, the compaction marker now moves past partial summaries, so OpenCode stops sending nearly the whole conversation every turn. Edits to `cache_ttl` now reach running sessions (#624), and on OpenCode 2 the dreamer runs on its schedule (#627) and per-model execute thresholds apply (#622). The release also fixes several unnecessary prompt-cache rewrites, makes smart-note checks more robust, and lowers the cost of each pass on large sessions. OpenCode 2 history commands now work with pure-v2 stores, tool errors survive `/compact`, and the historian works on Pi 1.0.

## Upgrading

- **The database moves from schema v94 to v95.** The migration runs the first time the new version opens `context.db`. It adds indexes for cleanup, retention and search reads, removes indexes that duplicate others, adds a lookup table for git commit search, and moves stored idle-gap marker decisions into their own table. On a 6.2 GB copy of a real database, the migration itself took about 1.4 seconds and that first start about 3.2 seconds.
- **Quit every OpenCode, OpenCode 2 and Pi process before restarting any of them.** They all share one database, including instances in other projects. While a process on an older version is still running, the new version refuses to migrate. After the migration, a host still on an older version refuses to open the v95 database, and downgrading the plugin does not downgrade the database.
- **OpenCode 2 still needs 2.0.22 or newer.** On an older OpenCode 2, Magic Context stays off and refuses every turn with a notice asking you to upgrade. OpenCode 2 does not install plugin updates on its own: open `/plugins`, select Magic Context and press ctrl+u, or run `opencode plugin update`.
- **Rust transform mode (experimental): use the `ck-mc` from this release.** v95 changes the indexes on two tables that `ck-mc` writes, so an older `ck-mc` refuses to write history summaries and user-memory candidates to the migrated database.
- **Remove `smart_drops` from your config.** The setting is deprecated and ignored because smart drops are now always on. A config that still contains it loads normally, and `doctor` reports a config warning until you remove it.
- **If the upgrade stops with a message about the git commit search map,** stop every host and run `magic-context doctor git-fts-map --repair`. It backs up `context.db` and `store.db` first and rebuilds only that map. Without `--repair`, the command only reports what it finds.

## New

- **`protected_tools`: keep the newest results of chosen tools** (#621, requested by @tenshiak). A map from tool name to a count, for example `"protected_tools": { "ask_user": 3 }`, keeps the newest N completed results of each named tool out of every automatic drop, at any context pressure. The defaults are `todowrite: 1` and `ctx_reduce: 3`; your user and project maps are merged over them, and `0` turns protection off for a tool. Tool names are case-insensitive and ignore a leading `mcp_`. A `ctx_reduce` or historian drop that targets a protected result waits until newer calls push it out of the protected count. Protection does not stop the historian: when that part of the conversation is summarized, the raw result leaves with it. If protected results alone cannot fit the model's context window, the turn is refused with an explanation instead of being sent over the limit. This applies on OpenCode, Pi and the Rust module.
- **Smart drops are always on.** Tool output that a later call has made obsolete is now removed for everyone: older edits to the same file are shortened to a marker that keeps the file path, and spent `todowrite`, `ctx_reduce` and status outputs are dropped. This happens only on passes that already rebuild the prompt cache, so it never causes a cache rewrite on its own; a session that had smart drops off catches up on its first such pass.
- **OpenCode 1, Rust transform mode: the compaction marker now advances.** Rust-mode summaries usually end partway through a message, and a safety check kept OpenCode's compaction marker from moving past those ends, so OpenCode sent nearly the whole conversation (thousands of messages on long sessions) every turn, slowing every pass. The marker now moves past ends that the next summary covers, never past content that has not been summarized, and only on passes that already rebuild the cache. When a pass cannot prove that the shortened request fits, the move waits for a later rebuild. If a pass fails after it may have moved the marker, that turn is refused and the next turn rebuilds the request instead of resending stale data.
- **`cache_ttl` edits apply to running sessions** (#624, reported by @null-axiom). User and project `cache_ttl` settings now take effect on the next pass in OpenCode, Pi and the Rust module; only the built-in defaults stay fixed per session. Raising the TTL keeps the cached prefix; lowering it rebuilds only after the normal idle expiry. `/ctx-status` now says whether the TTL comes from your config or from the built-in default.
- **OpenCode 2: the dreamer runs on its schedule** (#627, reported by @ICEY16360). The dreamer's schedule timer never started on OpenCode 2, so dream tasks ran only after a session finished a turn. The timer now starts on OpenCode 2 and stops when OpenCode 2 shuts down or reloads the project. A scheduled run uses the most recent session in that project folder; if there is none yet, tasks that need a session wait for their next scheduled time, and the other tasks still run. On OpenCode 2 the timer does not yet clean up stored data for deleted sessions.
- **The dashboard ships separately** and has its own release notes.

## Changes

- **OpenCode subagents no longer get `ctx_memory` and `ctx_note`.** Memories and notes belong to the primary session, so these tools are hidden from subagents on OpenCode 1 and 2, and a subagent call to either is refused. `ctx_search`, `ctx_expand` and `ctx_reduce` stay available, the primary session's tool list does not change, and Pi is unchanged.
- **More varied historian calibration examples.** The historian now sees three built-in example summaries, three older summaries from the session chosen for a spread of importance scores, and the session's four most recent summaries without their scores, so the scores it gives new summaries lean less on recent ones.
- **Files are created owner-only everywhere.** The Rust module (`ck-mc`), `setup`, `doctor`, database repair and the dashboard now create Magic Context's files as 0600 and directories as 0700, as the plugin already did, and your user `magic-context.jsonc` ends up 0600 when one of them rewrites it. In Rust transform mode the shared data directory stays owner-only even with `storage.enforce_private_permissions: false`.
- **SQLite now syncs less often on Pi, the CLI and the Rust module.** These writers use SQLite's NORMAL sync mode with its write-ahead log, as OpenCode on Bun already did. In a measured run of 32 writes, the total time spent holding the write lock fell from about 4.1 ms to 0.25 ms. After a power failure or operating-system crash, the most recent writes can be lost, but the database stays consistent.
- **OpenCode 1.18.32 and newer adopt a system-prompt change on the request whose messages are final.** The new system prompt is already sent on that request, so Magic Context no longer schedules another rebuild that would rewrite the provider cache a second time.
- **The Rust historian input names its raw message range.** It now includes a `Messages X-Y:` header, matching the TypeScript historian input even when some messages are omitted from the prompt.
- **Rust transform mode waits for an execute pass to publish the first historian result into an append-only prompt.** A historian finishing below the execute threshold no longer forces an early rewrite of the warm prompt prefix.
- **Configured model variants reach Rust-mode historian and dreamer requests.** The Rust module now sends each configured chain model's variant, including fallback models, instead of using the provider default.
- **The OpenCode plugin no longer installs its own copy of Solid and OpenTUI.** OpenCode's TUI already provides them to plugins, so `solid-js`, `@opentui/core` and `@opentui/solid` are now optional peer dependencies. This removes two critical advisories in `seroval` (GHSA-p6vx-979v-rg4c, GHSA-jp82-f5mq-hwhp) from the installed package. The sidebar and status dialog render as before on OpenCode 1 and OpenCode 2.
- **The dreamer recognizes a provider's quota notice.** Some auth plugins answer an exhausted account with a short message instead of an error. Magic Context now treats that as a provider failure, uses your configured fallback model, and skips the exhausted model for the rest of that run until its reset time. `/ctx-status` shows when the primary model's quota resets.

## Fixes

- **OpenCode 2: `/ctx-wrapup` and `/ctx-recomp` work with pure-v2 stores** (#629, reported by @isilveirascsimdigital). Both commands now use the OpenCode 2 history and compaction paths instead of attempting a v1-only database write.
- **OpenCode 2: tool errors survive `/compact`** (#631, reported by @moynzzz). Compacted requests keep both the error status and the error text for earlier tool calls.
- **Pi: historian runs on Pi 1.0** (#633, reported by @WhaleFell). Plain Pi no longer reads Oh My Pi's host tool registry while its extension runtime is loading, which could fail historian and recomp runs.
- **Search no longer returns memories already shown in forced folds.** OpenCode 1 and Pi now track the memories rendered in both history blocks, so `ctx_search` excludes memories already visible in the updates block.
- **Pi keeps the measured last-good request across append-only recaptures.** New messages appended to a previously measured request no longer discard its provider-measured size, reducing false over-window refusals.
- **Writes stop when another machine holds the session's agent checkout.** OpenCode 1, OpenCode 2 and Pi now refuse the turn with an explanation rather than writing session state for an agent checked out elsewhere.
- **Subagents apply queued drops at the execute threshold** (#619, reported by @dhaern). A subagent's queued `ctx_reduce` drops and other queued cleanup waited until its context reached the force band. They now apply on the subagent's passes at the execute threshold. Primary sessions are unchanged. This applies on OpenCode, Pi and the Rust module.
- **OpenCode 2: per-model execute thresholds apply** (#622, reported by @Tahmid-kabir-addin). Per-model entries in `execute_threshold_percentage` and `execute_threshold_tokens` were ignored on OpenCode 2, so every session used `default` to decide when queued drops run and when the historian starts. OpenCode 1 and Pi were not affected.
- **`ctx_reduce` no longer drops `ctx_reduce` calls** (#623, reported by @Sugaroverdose). A model could ask `ctx_reduce` to drop the tag of its own `ctx_reduce` call, see the context unchanged because the newest tags are protected, and repeat the same reply in a loop. A request to drop the tag of a `ctx_reduce` call is now skipped with one sentence in the tool result explaining that these calls are cleaned up automatically; the other requested tags still apply.
- **Note reminders no longer rewrite cached messages.** A reminder about pending notes could be added to a user message that had already been sent, rewriting the cached prefix from that point (about 147,000 tokens in one measured case). Reminders are now added only to a new user message the first time it is sent, or on a pass that already rebuilds the cache. This applies on OpenCode, Pi and the Rust module.
- **Pi: idle-gap time markers stay put after a history cut.** After Pi removed old history, the next pass could drop a time marker such as `+5m` from an earlier user message, rewriting about 186,000 cached tokens in one measured case. Each message's marker decision is now stored and replayed on later passes, and markers for new messages are decided only on a pass that rebuilds the cache.
- **Rust transform mode: a held replay is no longer released early.** After a pass falls back to the last good request, Rust mode keeps sending those exact bytes. 0.45.0 ended that hold after a set number of passes or new messages, and a counting error could end it on the very next healthy pass, so earlier messages that were already cached changed. The hold now lasts until a pass that rebuilds the cache anyway, or until the held request is no longer safe to send, and new messages reach the module as small updates in the meantime. If both the held request and the module's output are known to be over the model's limit, the turn is refused instead.
- **Fallback resends are judged on the provider's measured size.** When Magic Context resends the last good request because the current pass failed, it now uses the provider's measured size of that request plus an estimate for the new messages, instead of re-estimating the whole request. A large session could otherwise be refused at an estimate well above its real size. This applies on OpenCode 1 and 2.
- **Rust transform mode: `ctx_search` with a date range finds older matches.** Date filters were applied after each source's 100-result cap, so older matches inside the range could be hidden behind 100 newer ones.
- **Smart notes wait out GitHub rate limits instead of parking public repositories.** Compile dry-runs and scheduled checks now recognize GitHub's secondary rate-limit responses as well as reset and Retry-After headers, and retry later without counting a failure. Warnings that a check could not run are marked as delivered once shown, so they do not repeat on later turns. This applies on OpenCode and Pi.
- **Smart-note checks no longer time out on slow sites.** A check could be stopped after 2 seconds while its web request was allowed 5, so a slow GitHub answer failed the check and, after three such failures, downgraded a healthy note. Checks now get the full request time, and a network timeout is retried later without counting as a failure.
- **Smart-note checks can no longer hang the dreamer.** A check waiting on a host call, such as a web request, that ignored cancellation could hold up the whole sweep and the dreamer task; every such call now ends at the check's deadline. A slow start of the check sandbox no longer cuts into a check's own time limits, and a sandbox that fails to load within 10 seconds leaves the check for the next sweep without counting a failure.
- **Startup right after a migration no longer races the migration's cleanup.** The migration reported that it had finished before closing its database connection, so a host that read the database immediately could fail with a "database is busy" error.

## Performance

- **Pi batches heuristic tool-removal bookkeeping.** On cleanup passes that remove many tools, Pi now prepares native removal markers in one transaction instead of writing once per tool.
- **Fold preparation holds the write lock for less time.** Rendering the main history summary and preparing drop conversions happen before writer admission; rendering the history-update delta and writing the cached prompt remain together under the lock.
- **OpenCode 1 execute passes avoid log-only host reads and full tag loads.** They no longer wait for permission reads used only for logging, and pending drops load only the tags they need instead of the session's full tag history.
- **Shorter database lock holds after a history summary.** Choosing which drops to queue after the historian publishes now happens before taking the write lock, so other sessions' turns no longer wait behind it. This applies on OpenCode and Pi.
- **Faster, bounded compaction-marker writes on OpenCode 1.** The check before writing the compaction boundary into OpenCode's database now uses the per-message index (1.7 seconds to under 1 ms on a session with a million parts), and the write waits at most 250 ms for OpenCode's own writer before retrying on the next rebuild. Removing a marker keeps its longer wait.
- **Faster passes and lower memory on large sessions.** Repeated work on each pass is reused or skipped: token measurements of unchanged messages, Pi's session snapshots and history lookups, and checks for queued drops. Per-turn state now keeps small flags instead of the streamed message content: 3.7 MB instead of 121 MB on a 60,000-message test session. Pi also releases a session's cached content when the session closes.
- **Fewer database reads and writes.** Opening the database no longer takes the write lock when there is nothing to update; with another process holding that lock, an open fell from 286 ms to under 1 ms. On OpenCode 2, Magic Context reads OpenCode's storage less often and skips state writes that would not change anything. The new v95 indexes speed up cleanup, retention and git commit search.
- **Faster `doctor` on large databases.** The check for projects split across two identities fell from 1.3 seconds to 70 ms on 60,000 sessions in one directory.

## Internal

- Release, CI and test infrastructure, the Rust module's role catalogs and model-runner client for CortexKit's own tooling, and design and measurement reports. None of these change behavior in OpenCode or Pi.

name: Dashboard dashboard-v0.19.0
body:
## Dashboard v0.19.0

A redesigned configuration page. Works with Magic Context 0.45.x.

### A clearer Config page
The configuration form is reorganised into eight sections with an index on the left: General, Context window, History, Memory & search, Background models, Dreamer schedule, Prompt surface and Advanced. Each section is a single column of settings, with the explanation on the left and the control on the right. Below about 1,000 pixels wide, rows stack so controls keep their full width. Raw config keys are hidden unless you turn on "Show config keys", and settings that need a restart are marked.

### Pickers instead of free text
- **Output language** is a searchable list of languages, for example "Turkish (tr)".
- **Variants** for the historian and dreamer models offer the variants the selected model supports. If they're unknown, you can still type one.
- **The cue compressor model** uses the same model picker as the historian and dreamer.
- **Fallback models** each get a full row: model, variant and remove. The model list opens above the page instead of being cut off.

### Forms instead of JSON boxes
- **Model routes** are a table of route and preset.
- **Tool descriptions** list each Magic Context tool with its built-in text. Edit one to override it, or reset it to the default; only the ones you change are saved.
- **Pi subagent extensions** are a list with one entry per row.

### Help next to each setting
The "How it works" expanders are now a small "?" button beside the setting. It opens a short explanation with a link to the matching page of the documentation, which opens in your browser.

### Other changes
- Per-model cache TTL and threshold overrides sit in one collapsible table.
- The dreamer schedule is a compact table of tasks and their schedules.
- The Auto Update setting shows its real default instead of "undefined".
- A dreamer task that was skipped, or refused before reaching the model, says so on its card instead of showing a provider error.
- Config files the dashboard writes are readable only by your user account.

name: v0.45.0
body:
This release makes `context.db` the one database Magic Context keeps its data in, and lowers what each turn costs: reasoning from older turns now leaves the request on every provider, emergency drops skip passes that would save almost nothing, and a turn writes far less to disk. A pass that fails partway no longer sends the conversation without its reductions. Agents can recover a dropped item by its tag, and Pi's status displays stop showing raw estimates as usage. On OpenCode 2 it now needs 2.0.22 or newer, the dreamer's curate task works there again, and its retrospective task runs there for the first time. It also carries a long list of fixes across caching, compression, Pi, the CLI, config handling and search.

## Upgrading

- **The database moves from schema v91 to v94.** Three migrations run the first time the new version opens `context.db`: v92 records the database's single-store state and adds boundary columns to compartments, v93 tracks a history revision per session, and v94 stores each session's last good request in pieces instead of one record that grew on every turn. On a 7.5 GB database the first start took about 6 to 45 seconds longer than usual, almost all of it v94, and later starts are normal. The migration now runs on a separate thread, so OpenCode keeps answering while it works, including the `/health` checks that supervisors such as OpenChamber use.
- **Quit every OpenCode and Pi process before starting the new version.** This includes OpenCode 1 and OpenCode 2 servers, Pi and OMP processes, and instances in other projects, because they all share the database. While a process on an older version is still running, the new version refuses to migrate, and its turns fail with OpenCode's generic "Unexpected server error" (the reason is in the Magic Context log). Once every old process has quit, start the new version. After the migration, 0.44.4 and earlier refuse the v94 database, and downgrading the plugin does not downgrade the database.
- **Expect a cache rebuild on a session's first turn after upgrading.** The guidance and tool descriptions sent to the model changed. A session usually rebuilds its cached prefix once; one that resumes from a saved request may do so on a later turn instead.
- **Rust transform mode (experimental) needs a one-time offline migration.** `ck-mc` now refuses a store that has not been moved into `context.db`, with `MC-C14`: "Magic Context's Rust mode needs a one-time migration of its store. Quit OpenCode and every ck-mc process, then run `magic-context doctor single-store migrate`." The command backs up both databases first. To roll back, restore `ck-mc` together with `context.db` and `store.db` from that backup.
- **OpenCode 2 needs 2.0.22 or newer.** Magic Context creates and deletes its background sessions through the session API that OpenCode 2.0.22 added. On an older OpenCode 2 it stays off and refuses every turn before anything reaches the model, with a notice: "Magic Context is disabled: OpenCode 2.0.22 or newer is required (session.remove and session.compact). Upgrade OpenCode and restart." It never sends a turn it hasn't prepared. `doctor` prints the requirement next to the OpenCode version it finds.
- **OpenCode 2** does not install plugin updates on its own. Open `/plugins`, select Magic Context and press ctrl+u, or run `opencode plugin update`.

## One database

- **`context.db` is the only authoritative store.** In Rust transform mode, memories, notes, compartments and session state now live in `context.db`, shared with the plugin, instead of being copied between `context.db` and the module's own `store.db`. `store.db` keeps only caches that can be rebuilt. OpenCode and Pi without Rust mode already used `context.db` and need no action beyond the restart above.
- **`doctor single-store`** migrates the store (`migrate`; `--prefer-history <session>=store|context` picks which copy of a session's history to keep) and restores a session history the migration left incomplete from its backup (`repair-history --from-backup <dir>`).
- **Installs with no host** (only `ck-mc`) get a database with `npx @cortexkit/magic-context doctor store init`, which setup now runs. Without it, `ck-mc` refuses with `MC-C15`.

## Lower costs

- **Old reasoning leaves the request on every provider.** Reasoning from older turns was only cleared on Anthropic routes. It is now removed, with its provider metadata such as OpenAI's encrypted reasoning, on OpenAI, Vertex, Bedrock, OpenRouter and other routes too. The newest assistant turn keeps its reasoning.
- **Models whose reasoning must stay a contiguous run** (Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, on any route) have the oldest reasoning trimmed from the front, so the provider never sees a gap that invalidates the rest.
- **Dropping a tool call or message also removes the reasoning tied to it** on every provider, instead of writing `[cleared]` into the reasoning text.
- **Emergency drops skip passes that would reclaim less than 2,000 tokens.** Before, a pass could rewrite a 300K-token prefix, and lose its cache, to save under 200 tokens.
- **Far fewer disk writes per turn.** The last good request and replay decisions are now stored in pieces, so a turn no longer rewrites a record that grows with the session. On a large session, writes per new-message pass fell from about 3.6 MB to about 0.1 MB, and `ck-mc`'s own writes fell by a similar factor.
- **Faster passes on large sessions.** A whitespace check scanned every tag in the session on each pass; on a measured large session the median new-message pass went from 780 ms to 100 ms. Rust mode caches its compartment boundary checks between passes.
- **Identical parallel reads are deduplicated.** Duplicate-tool cleanup only knew MCP-prefixed tool names, so it never matched OpenCode's and Pi's own `read`, `grep` and `glob`. When one reply makes the same call twice, the older copy is now dropped on the next pass that rebuilds the cache anyway, and a protected newest copy no longer keeps an older one alive.
- **A restart no longer re-splits embedded history.** After every start, the first check of which history still needed embedding tokenized the whole session's text again. Magic Context now records how each compartment was split and skips that work while the text is unchanged (#604).

## A failed pass is never sent unmanaged

- **The last good request is replayed, or the turn is refused.** When a stage that changes the request fails (for example, tagging under a busy database), Magic Context used to continue and could send the conversation without its drops, once 2.5 times larger than the turn before. It now sends the last good request again or refuses the turn with `MC-S06`: "This request was not sent: Magic Context could not finish preparing it, and without that preparation it could be far larger than the previous request. Send your message again."
- **A request estimated above the context limit is refused** when its pass was degraded in a way that could change or grow it. Pi refuses the same way instead of falling through to the raw history.

## For agents

- **`ctx_expand tag=N` recovers an item by its tag.** It accepts the number from a `§N§` prefix or a `[dropped §N§]` placeholder and returns that text or tool call, including dropped ones. Before, agents passed the tag to `message=`, which counts raw messages and often recovered a neighbouring item (#585).
- **Explicit self-tagging guidance.** Where tag prefixes are shown, the guidance now tells the agent to start each reply that has text with the next tag number, and that a reply of only tool calls gets none. This makes the stored text of a reply match what the provider returned more often, which routes that continue from earlier replies need (#582).
- **Tool descriptions match what the tools do (#575).** `ctx_search` says an empty `sources` list searches everything and lists `primer`; `ctx_note` says an omitted filter includes pending smart notes and that reads take at most 50 IDs; `ctx_memory` no longer advertises a `limit` it ignores.

## OpenCode 2

- **Background sessions use OpenCode's own lifecycle.** Each historian and dreamer run gets a new session, under your session when there is one, and Magic Context deletes it through OpenCode's session API when the run ends. Background sessions that earlier versions recorded for reuse are deleted in small batches at startup (#589, #594).
- **Background runs survive OpenCode compacting them.** When a historian or dreamer prompt was large enough for OpenCode 2 to compact its new session before the first step, Magic Context no longer recognised its own prompt and refused every run with `hidden_prompt_unrecognized`. Those runs now go through.
- **The retrospective task runs on OpenCode 2.** It had no way to read OpenCode 2 history, found nothing, and still reported success. Manual and scheduled runs now read your messages from OpenCode 2's store (#602).
- **Skipped tasks are recorded as skipped, on every host.** A dreamer task that cannot run (`compress-cues` with mural off, a retrospective with no history source, a Pi model chain with no available model, or a run held back by the single-store migration) now shows as skipped with its reason in run summaries and `/ctx-status`, not as a success (#602).
